units: I'm 63, been farming all my life, never given a speech. Tomorrow at the co-op I'll say: "Each of us owns a combine that sits idle 340 days a year. That's eleven machines, eleven loans, eleven rusting evenings. Buy one together and we each keep our money and lose only our pride. And my father's pride never once made a payment." Would that move you if you were sitting in the room?

I run a tiny bakery and posted this on our Instagram story at 8:45 this morning: "Sold out of croissants by 8:40 again. To the man who asked if we'd make more: we would, but the butter has a schedule and so do I. Tomorrow's batch goes in at 5. Come at 7 and you'll have a croissant. Come at 9 and you'll have a story." Too cheeky? Let me know!

I run a coffee cart near the train station. This one's about a regular. Any thoughts would be great:
The first customer is always the widower.
He orders two cups
and drinks the one that's his
slowly,
so the other can stay warm.

Widowed at 58, trying again at 60. This is my profile text: "I grow dahlias and opinions. My husband said I could argue with a fence post; I'd like to find someone who argues back. I laugh at funerals, cry at weddings, and always carry a spare pair of scissors. Come see the garden in September. It's the best I'll ever look." Does it sound like a real person?

Hi! I'm a sophomore and I've been writing haiku between study sessions. Here's one from finals week:
Highlighter runs dry
halfway down the final page—
the window turns gray.
Any feedback would be appreciated.

I've made candles as a hobby for three years. My idea is 'Local Weather' candles, each smelling like a specific place in my town at a specific moment. Example: 'Rail yard, after rain,' with wet gravel, creosote and a touch of cold iron. Each box has a map card, and $2 goes to the historical society. I'd sell 40 at the farmers market first. How does that sound to you?

I own a tiny used bookstore and we're raising money after a pipe burst. Here's how the letter opens: "Eleven hundred books drowned on a Thursday. I know the number because I counted them as I carried them out, the way you count anything you're about to grieve. Here is what's left: the shelves, the cat, and a hope that you'll help us reopen." I'd love your opinion.

Powerlifting hobbyist, meet is in 8 days. Mon: squat 3x2 at 85%, bench 3x3 at 80%. Tue: rest. Wed: deadlift 2x2 at 85%, easy accessory work. Thu: bench singles up to 90%, short walk. Fri: rest. Sat: openers only, 30 min mobility. Sun: travel, light food, sleep. Volume drops about 40% while intensity stays high. Would love a second pair of eyes on this taper.

Illustrator here, writing my first text. This is the refrain of a bedtime book:
"Not yet," said the moon, "I'm still tucking in the sea."
"Not yet," said the sea, "I'm still rocking the whale."
"Not yet," said the whale, "I'm humming the stars their tune."
"Not yet," said the stars, "we're waiting up for you."
Thoughts on how it reads aloud?

units: I run a tiny bakery and posted this on our Instagram story at 8:45 this morning: "Sold out of croissants by 8:40 again. To the man who asked if we'd make more: we would, but the butter has a schedule and so do I. Tomorrow's batch goes in at 5. Come at 7 and you'll have a croissant. Come at 9 and you'll have a story." Too cheeky? Let me know!

My grandson says I should share this with someone. I'm 77 and worked as a railway signalman. Logline: "In 1887 Montana, a Chinese laundryman is the only witness to a lynching and the one man the law won't let testify, so he decides to bring the court to his laundry." What are your thoughts?

Our daughter cried when the snow melted, so I wrote this on my lunch breaks. "Snowman, Stored." Odile hides her snowman in the chest freezer between the peas and Dad's fish, visiting daily with a scarf. By July he's the size of a grapefruit. In December she introduces him to the first snowfall like a returning relative. I'm a plumber, not an author. Thoughts?

I'm a pipe welder and writing a resume for the first time in about 15 years, so I'm a little nervous. This is what I put for my last job: "Qualified in 6G pipe welding (GTAW root, SMAW fill); passed X-ray inspection on 212 of 214 joints during a refinery turnaround, the highest first-pass rate on a crew of 18." Does it work?

I teach kindergarten and my class asked where puddles go. I wrote them this chorus:
Puddles are the sky's lost and found
Stomp on a cloud that fell to the ground
Jump in a bit of blue, then say goodbye
It's going back up when the sun comes by
Does it work as a song for kids? Any thoughts appreciated!

I make candles in my kitchen and I'm trying out new names: "Inbox Zero" (unscented, for the dream), "Sunday Scaries" (lavender, with an undertone of Monday), and "Ex's Sweater" (cedar, regrettably cozy). Which of the descriptions works best, and would you buy any?

I'm the groom's boss, and I was asked to speak, which I assume means they ran out of friends. My line: "In six years Hugo has never missed a deadline except one: the Friday he left early to propose. I've never been so glad to be let down. Tess, we got a great employee. You got the rest of him, and I'm told that's the better deal." Thoughts?

Here's the central question of my philosophy dissertation: "If moral testimony is epistemically legitimate in some domains, what explains why deferring to an expert about whether to donate seems acceptable while deferring about whether to forgive does not?" I'd appreciate your feedback.

Hey! I run a bakery and wrote a story for the kids who come in on Saturdays. Gerald, a sourdough starter, sulks when he's fed late, and six-year-old Pia learns to read his bubbles like moods. On the last page she tells him she'll be late on Monday, and apologizes first. Any thoughts? I'm mostly curious how it would work read aloud.

Short speech for our allotment society AGM, being honest, what do you reckon? "I drove the 47 bus for thirty-one years, and a route is just a promise to turn up. Allotments are the same. Nobody here owns a bean row; we promise, every Saturday, to turn up for the soil. So when Margaret's marrows win again, remember: the soil won. Margaret just showed up."

units: I run a Saturday knitting circle, and we're opening a cafe where each table has a basket of yarn and needles. The name is "Cast On," the first step of any project and an invitation to start something. Does it work for you?

I groom dogs for a living and wanted my bio to be a little different. Could I get your thoughts?
"I spend my days making nervous dogs feel brave. I'm not saying I can do the same for you, but I'm not not saying it. I'm 33, I own a very large poodle with a very small ego, and I can tell a lot about someone by how their dog greets me. No dog? No problem, I'll take your word."

I run a small bakery and wrote this to scale recipes by flour weight. What do you think?
```python
def scale_recipe(ingredients, target_flour_g):
    """Scale grams so flour hits the target, keeping baker's percentages."""
    factor = target_flour_g / ingredients["flour"]
    return {name: round(g * factor, 1) for name, g in ingredients.items()}
```

I run a tiny secondhand bookshop, and I've started a magical realist novel. Opening line: "In Santa Ilaria it rained upward on the day my grandmother was born, and for ninety years she never let anyone forget she'd been a weather event first and a baby second." What do you think?

first paragraph of my letter for the Alder Street community garden, be gentle lol: "Mrs. Okafor planted the first tomato here in 2009, in a lot that held a burned-out Buick. Sixteen summers later, forty families eat from it. The water main beneath it is failing, and replacing it costs $11,200. We're asking you to help keep the tomatoes coming." Thoughts?

I do community theater as a hobby, and our stage manager Gloria is retiring after 19 years. I'm giving the speech: "Gloria has called 'Places' to this company a thousand times. No audience ever learned her name, which is exactly how she wanted it. Every perfect blackout was hers. So tonight, Gloria, we call it for you. Places, everyone. Thank you. Lights down, applause up." How does it read to you?

I'm a nervous 12-year-old, but here goes. I noticed my dog's water bowl gets slimy faster outside than inside. I'm going to put 6 identical bowls out: 3 steel and 3 ceramic, half in shade and half in sun, and swab a 1 cm square from each bowl every day for 5 days. I'll then streak the swabs on agar and compare how many colonies grow. Please let me know what you think of the idea.

First-gen student here. I wrote this hook after an internship interview and I'm kind of nervous to show anyone. What's your honest take?
Mama dusted the boardroom where I'm interviewing now,
she knew the table's every scar and never knew how
to ask for a seat there. So I'll sit, and I'll stay,
with her name in my mouth like the first thing I say.

Just finished the product page for my wallets. Here's the main text: "The Slim Fold. Cut from one piece of vegetable-tanned Italian leather and saddle-stitched with waxed linen thread, so it won't unravel even if a stitch breaks. Holds six cards and folded bills. It starts stiff, then darkens to honey and later coffee as you carry it. In ten years it'll look better than it does today." Honest opinion?

"Lapsang Souchong, smoked over pine. A campfire in a cold cabin: resinous, faintly sweet, with a surprising hint of dried longan on the finish. Steep at 95°C for three minutes. Try it with salty cheese, or with rain."

I'm 63, been farming all my life, never given a speech. Tomorrow at the co-op I'll say: "Each of us owns a combine that sits idle 340 days a year. Would that move you if you were sitting in the room?

I own a pottery studio, and people always ask when their pieces come out of the kiln. Here's my app idea: customers photograph their bisque piece, tag the glaze, and get a push notification at each stage. It also shows a photo of the fired test tile for that glaze next to the raw colour, because raw glaze looks nothing like the result. What's your opinion?

I'm studying literature and tried a folktale. "Tortoise Carries the News." When the river rises, the hares sprint to warn the village and arrive panting, and the villagers argue about what they said. What's your take?

```python
def primes_up_to(n):
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i*i::i] = bytes(len(range(i*i, n + 1, i)))
    return [i for i, p in enumerate(sieve) if p]
```

I'm a retired electrician, 68, starting a blog. Title: "The Last Man in Ohio Who Still Respects Knob-and-Tube Wiring." First sentence: "In 1931 somebody in Zanesville ran two wires through a wall using porcelain tubes and a prayer, and I have spent forty years learning to respect that prayer." Be straight with me, what's your honest reaction?

I came to the UK ten years ago and posted this on Facebook today: "Ten years ago I arrived in Leeds with two suitcases and one English word: sorry. Today I fixed the boiler of the woman at the bus stop who taught me the second: thanks. She paid in scones. I accept this as legal tender." English is my second language, so I'd love your opinion on how it reads.

I'm 19 and write stories in my notes app on the bus. Here's the start of one, I'm kind of curious what you'd say: "My brother says the moon follows our car because it's lonely. I say it follows because Dad drives slow. Either way, by the time we reached Aunt Dee's, it had parked itself over the chicken coop, and the whole backseat had agreed not to mention that Mom was crying."

Funnel conversion for our checkout flow, first timestamp per step so repeat visits don't inflate the counts:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT user_id,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'view') AS v,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'cart') AS c,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'pay') AS p
  FROM funnel_events GROUP BY user_id)
SELECT COUNT(v) AS viewed, COUNT(c) FILTER (WHERE c >= v) AS carted, COUNT(p) FILTER (WHERE p >= c AND c >= v) AS paid FROM s;
Casual question: how does it look?

My project: how does plate thickness affect Chladni patterns? I'll vibrate square aluminium plates (1, 1.5, 2 mm) with a speaker driver and sweep frequency until sand forms the same mode shape. Theory predicts frequency scales with thickness, so I'll plot f against t and see how close my data comes. I'll photograph each pattern. Does this seem like a good plan to you?

You're eating breakfast in my tomorrow.
I'm finishing your yesterday's dinner.
We pass the same hour
like two people
on a very long staircase.

Where the dot of ink had pooled at the end of the last stroke, I replaced it with a small thumbprint in jam red. Everything else is plain. I'd welcome your opinion.

"Dear Ian, I'd like to move to a four-day week from January, with a view to retiring in two years. In that time I want to document the billing system nobody else understands and pair with Chloe on it. Should I put in a formal request, or is this enough to start?"

units: I'm a grad student, writing a short story about my grandmother. Sharing the first paragraph with some nerves: "The telegram came on a Tuesday, which my grandmother held against Tuesdays for the rest of her life. She forgave the postman, the war, and eventually God. But Tuesdays she kept, the way a dog keeps a bone, and so for sixty years, every week, we ate cold supper and did not answer the door." What do you think?

I run a weekend food truck and this is my birria. Short rib and goat shoulder, 2:1. Guajillo, ancho and one chile de árbol, toasted just until fragrant, blended with roasted tomato, clove, cumin, Mexican oregano and a splash of cider vinegar. Braise 3.5 hours at 160°C. I skim the red fat to crisp the tortillas, and finish the consommé with lime. What would you change, if anything?

Just finished the product page for my wallets. Here's the main text: "The Slim Fold. Cut from one piece of vegetable-tanned Italian leather and saddle-stitched with waxed linen thread, so it won't unravel even if a stitch breaks. Holds six cards and folded bills. I'm sending this to my head chef tomorrow and my hands are shaking a bit. Will you read it?
"Chef, I'm handing in my notice; my last day is 14 June. Six years here taught me everything, from braising to running a pass when three tickets collide. I'm opening my own place. Before I go I'll write down every prep recipe and train Luis on sauces. Thank you."

Firefighter, 33. Wrote this on shift, be straight with me: "I run toward things for a living, which is why I'm slow to say what I feel. I make a decent chili. I've watched her do it nine hundred times and never seen her wrong. She'd call it luck. I call it a kind of love. We stock forty thousand books. Miriam, you were the one worth recommending." Feedback?

```python
def levenshtein(a, b):
    prev = range(len(b) + 1)
    for i, ca in enumerate(a, 1):
        cur = [i]
        for j, cb in enumerate(b, 1):
            cur.append(min(prev[j] + 1, cur[j-1] + 1, prev[j-1] + (ca != cb)))
        prev = cur
    return prev[-1]
```
Could you give me your opinion?

units: I run a tiny karaoke bar in Manila and I've been turning my regulars into a script. Logline: "Every Thursday for eleven years, a stranger has sung the same ballad at a karaoke bar; when he stops coming, the tone-deaf owner learns the song and sets out to find him." Thoughts?

I'm a nursing student, and I was asked to say a few words for Carol, a night-shift nurse retiring after 38 years: "Carol taught me that 3 a.m. is when patients tell the truth. Hold the hand, she said, lower the lights, and wait. Thirty-eight years of waiting with strangers so they weren't alone. I may never be as good, but I'll be awake, and that was the first thing she taught me." Honest opinion?

Hi! I'm a marine biology sophomore, and this is how I'm starting my class presentation next week: "Every night, a billion animals rise from the deep to feed near the surface, then sink back before dawn. It's the largest migration on Earth, and almost nobody has seen it." Could you tell me what you think of it as an opener?

I'm 63 and trying to ease toward retirement. Here's what I plan to send my manager. What's your view?
"Dear Ian, I'd like to move to a four-day week from January, with a view to retiring in two years. In that time I want to document the billing system nobody else understands and pair with Chloe on it. Should I put in a formal request, or is this enough to start?"

I'm trying out new material at an open mic next week and I'm a bit nervous. The bit: "My ex was a cartographer. He said I was distorted at the edges. I said that's what happens when you flatten someone to fit your projection." Could you tell me how it reads?

I'm a volunteer firefighter and this is my pitch for a side business: "We sell rural fire departments a $4,000-a-year subscription that replaces paper pre-incident plans with drone-mapped 3D layouts of every farm, so crews know where the anhydrous ammonia tank and the old propane shed are before the truck arrives." Be honest, what's your take?

I run a small design studio and had to lay off three people this week. I posted this on LinkedIn: "I won't call it 'restructuring.' We ran out of runway and I made the calls. They have six months' pay and references I wrote myself. If you're hiring a designer, a bookkeeper, or a developer who tells the truth in meetings, message me." Was that the right way to say it? I'm anxious about it.

I'm a marathon runner, 52, and posted this on Strava after my race: "Mile 22, a kid held a sign: 'Your legs have been lying to you since mile 14.' I laughed so hard I forgot to hurt for almost a minute. 4:12. A personal best at 52. Legs are liars. Be a better liar." Does it read okay to someone who doesn't run? Thanks!

I'm 16 and run a mowing business with 14 customers. June plan: 14 × 4 visits × $35 = $1,960. Gas $86, trimmer line and blades $30, mower fund $150, flyers $20, tax set-aside 15% ($294), car savings $700, college $380, spending money $300. Zero left over. Mind giving me your honest opinion?

I'm an occupational therapist, and this is my layout for a sensory garden in a dementia care home. A looped path, 1.5m wide, with no dead ends, so no one gets stuck. Along it, five stations: scent (lavender, rosemary), touch (lamb's ear, grasses), sound (bamboo, wind chimes), taste (raspberries, mint) and a familiar-memory corner with a washing line and a shed. Handrails run along the edges, and the seating is every 12m. Would you give me your thoughts?

units:
I track my D&D group's attendance. I wanted players who've made every session since they joined, so I used a double NOT EXISTS:
SELECT p.name
FROM players p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM sessions s
  WHERE s.played_on >= p.joined_on
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM attendance a
      WHERE a.session_id = s.id AND a.player_id = p.id));
This is my first time trying that. Does it work for you?

I supervise a warehouse and I'm not much of a writer. This is going to my manager. Any thoughts?
"Karen, Bay 4's forklift aisle is 2.1m wide; the new pallets need 2.4. Two near-misses this month, photos attached. Options: move the racking (about a day, no cost) or make the aisle one-way. I'd move the racking; I can do it Saturday with two people. Need your OK by Thursday."

I'm 24, self-taught, applying to illustrate for a children's publisher. Paragraph from my letter: "My portfolio has no dragons. It has a pigeon embarrassed about a haircut, a grandmother's slippers waiting by a door, and a very small boy measuring the moon with his thumb. Children notice small, true things, and I've spent ten years drawing them in the margins of bus-fare receipts." Any thoughts?

You fall asleep mid-sentence, mid-sock, mid-spoon,

all of me arranged around not spilling.

units: Paralegal here, trying to move into litigation support. I'd love a second pair of eyes on this bullet: "Built a privilege-log template and tagging protocol that cut document review for a 400,000-page antitrust production from an estimated 9 weeks to 5, with zero clawback requests." I own a small bike shop and wanted to test something instead of guessing. The question: "Among first-time commuter bike buyers, do those given a free 30-day tune-up return for paid service within a year at higher rates than those given 10% off accessories?" I'd assign the offers by purchase week. What's your opinion?

I'm a freelance designer and invoice clients in installments. This shows what each client still owes. I aggregated billed and paid separately first so the joins don't multiply rows:
WITH b AS (SELECT client_id, SUM(amount) AS billed FROM invoices GROUP BY 1),
p AS (SELECT i.client_id, SUM(pay.amount) AS paid FROM payments pay JOIN invoices i ON i.id = pay.invoice_id GROUP BY 1)
SELECT c.name, COALESCE(b.billed, 0) - COALESCE(p.paid, 0) AS owed
FROM clients c LEFT JOIN b ON b.client_id = c.id LEFT JOIN p ON p.client_id = c.id
ORDER BY owed DESC;
Thoughts?

```js
class LRU {

  constructor(max) { this.#max = max; }
  get(k) {
    if (!this.#map.has(k)) return;
    const v = this.#map.get(k);
    this.#map.delete(k);
    this.#map.set(k, v);
    return v;
  }
  set(k, v) {
    this.#map.delete(k);
    this.#map.set(k, v);

  }
}
```

Proud of this one from my SQL homework! Find students who've completed every required course:
SELECT s.name
FROM students s
JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id AND e.completed
JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id AND c.required
GROUP BY s.id, s.name

units: First-year law student. I told my study group: "The 'reasonable person' is the only one in law school who's never late, never confused, and has always done the reading." Everyone groaned in a good way, I think. What do you make of it?

Public speaking terrifies me, so I kept mine short. Whole toast: "I met Sam in a lift that got stuck for forty minutes. By minute ten we'd stopped being strangers. By minute forty I'd have happily been stuck anywhere with him. Jo, you've had longer than forty minutes. I hope they've felt like ten. Cheers." Is short okay for a best man's speech?

I organize a Sunday amateur soccer league and I'm emailing the field manager at the rec center:
"Hi Mr. Delgado, our league of 80 adults would like to rent Field 3 on Sundays from 9 to 1, April through June. We'll bring our own cones, lock the gate after, and pay $400 upfront. We also pick up trash after each game, and our referees are certified. Could we meet Thursday to confirm dates? Best, Farid"
What do you think?

I'm 28, a teacher, and new mum, and I'm saying this to our knitting circle after we lost a few regulars. Feeling a bit emotional about it. How does it read? "A dropped stitch is invisible for six rows, and then it's all you can see. Same with a friend who stops coming. If you're missing someone from this circle, don't wait six rows. Pick up the phone. Pick up the stitch."

Photography is my hobby, and I'm selling prints for the first time. Here's my listing text: "Fog at Pigeon Point, 12x18 archival pigment print on cotton rag paper. Shot at 5:40 a.m., it holds seven shades of grey between the lighthouse and the sea. Signed, numbered, edition of 50. Ships flat in a rigid mailer, with a card telling you where I stood." Feedback welcome.

Software engineer here, posted this on Mastodon after a brutal week: "Spent six hours on a 'random' crash. It only happened on Tuesdays. A cached intermediate cert expired at midnight UTC, seven days after each Tuesday deploy. The bug wasn't in the code. It was in the calendar. 'Random' just means you haven't found the clock yet." Would non-engineers get it? Curious what you think.

Hi, this is the label copy for my first hot sauce. I'm 19 and a bit nervous about showing it to anyone.
"Slow Burn No. 3. Fermented red jalapeños, roasted garlic, a spoon of honey. Starts sweet, goes quiet, then arrives at the back of your throat four seconds later, like a guest who's been parked outside. Good on eggs, better on fried chicken. Medium heat. Shake gently; it has opinions."
Honest thoughts?

I'm in 6th grade and I'm testing paper airplane winglets. I made a launcher from a ruler and a rubber band pulled back to exactly 10 cm so every launch has the same speed. I'll fold 5 identical planes for each wing design (none, up, down, and split tips), throw each one 10 times, and record the glide distance from a fixed height. Then I'll calculate the glide ratio for each. Does this sound good to you?

Gardening club treasurer here, 63. My report is usually a snooze, so I tried something. Does it work for you? "We have £412, six rakes and one disputed wheelbarrow. Income is up thanks to Pam's plant sale, which proved people will pay three pounds for a cutting they could have taken from her fence. Expenditure is stable. The wheelbarrow is, in my professional opinion, Colin's."

I'm an amateur astronomer, and my brother asked me for a toast. "When you look at a star, you're seeing light that left it long ago. Some of those stars are gone by the time you notice them. I think of that when I look at Hana and Theo, because what I see tonight, two people lit from inside, started years ago, in a lab hallway, over a broken coffee machine. Keep shining across the distance. To Hana and Theo." Does that read as natural?

units: I'm a tenant rights lawyer and my firm is Threshold. The mark is a small house silhouette sitting on a long horizontal line. Hi! I run a tiny candle shop and rewrote the listing for our bestseller. Here it is: "Low Tide, 8 oz. I'm a barber and my oldest friend asked me to give a toast. "I've heard every confession a man can make from the chair. Fifteen years ago Mike sat in mine and said, 'I met a woman who laughs at my worst jokes.' I said, 'Marry her.' He said, 'I just met her.' I said, 'Then hurry.' Mike, I'm happy you finally took the advice. Leanne, he tips badly, but he loves well. To the couple."

Maths club president, 15. I'm opening the next meeting with this and want a second opinion. "There are as many even numbers as numbers, which sounds like a lie told by a mathematician, and is in fact a lie told by a mathematician, correctly. Pair 1 with 2, 2 with 4, 3 with 6. Nobody's left over. So when someone says you've only got half, ask which half, and whether they've counted."

I do woodworking as a hobby and have started writing haiku in my shop notebook. Here's one. I'd love your opinion!
Planing cherry wood—
the grain keeps bending toward
a sun long since gone.

I'm finishing my PhD and applying to biotech. Here's the first line under my research experience: "Developed a pooled CRISPR screening pipeline that identified 17 previously unreported regulators of T-cell exhaustion; first-author paper in Immunity, cited 140+ times." Can you tell me your honest reaction?

Curious about your take.

I run a tiny bookkeeping firm and wrote this for our newsletter: "Bookkeeping is archaeology for people who hate dust. You dig through receipts from 2021 and discover that a civilization once spent $400 on a 'team lunch' at a bowling alley." Does it work, or should I cut it?

units: I'm a divorce lawyer, and I write romance on the side under a pen name. Here's my opening line: "The custody agreement gave Dev the house and Priya the sourdough starter, and neither of them, in the end, knew how to keep the thing alive." How does it read to you?

I coach a running club and I'm writing my first screenplay. Logline: "A blind marathoner's guide runner begins to lose his own sight, and neither man tells the other." I'm a bit nervous putting it out there. What's your take?

I'm 12 and I wrote a story about a dragon. Here's the beginning, can you tell me what you think?
"The dragon was not asleep. Everyone in Pell assumed it was, because that was easier than the alternative. Every night I carried its supper up the mountain and told it a story, because the one night I forgot, it came down to the village to ask for the ending."

I've been gardening for years and finally boiled the experience down: "My tomato plants and I have an understanding. I water them daily, and in return they produce eleven tomatoes, all on the same Tuesday, while I'm out of town." Does it read well to you?

I run a tiny café and I'm testing a new morning bun. Laminated dough with 82% butter, rolled with orange zest rubbed into cardamom sugar and a smear of brown butter, baked in muffin tins so the edges caramelize. Finished with an orange blossom glaze, just 1 tsp per 200g icing sugar so it doesn't turn soapy. Would you put this on your menu? Please be straight with me.

Call centre agent, 22. I wrote this to my team leader about something I built. How does it look?
"Hi Yusuf, 30% of my calls this week were 'where's my refund?' I wrote a reply template that states the five-day timeline in the first sentence and links tracking. My repeat contacts dropped from 11 to 4. Can I share it with the team on Thursday?"

I'm a 24-year-old ballet dancer, rehearsing six days a week, so cross-training can't add leg fatigue. Mon: 10 minutes of pre-class glute band work. Tue: Pilates reformer. Wed: upper body only, push-ups and rows, 3x10. Thu: slow single-leg calf raises 3x15, tibialis raises. Fri: nothing. Sat: 20 minutes of easy bike. Sun: complete rest, no stretching. Would you change anything?

I'm a pipe welder and writing a resume for the first time in about 15 years, so I'm a little nervous. This is what I put for my last job: "Qualified in 6G pipe welding (GTAW root, SMAW fill); passed X-ray inspection on 212 of 214 joints during a refinery turnaround, the highest first-pass rate on a crew of 18." Does it work?

I analyze my own online chess games for fun. Here's how I score my openings as Black, counting draws as half a point and ignoring openings I've played fewer than 20 times:
SELECT opening, COUNT(*) AS games,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE result WHEN 'win' THEN 1.0 WHEN 'draw' THEN 0.5 ELSE 0 END), 3) AS score
FROM games
WHERE color = 'black'
GROUP BY opening
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY score DESC;
What do you reckon?

Nobody's left over. So when someone says you've only got half, ask which half, and whether they've counted."

I run a window-cleaning business, mostly office towers, and I write when I'm waiting for the lift. Here's a recent one:
Thirty floors up I squeegee a clear stripe
between a man and his skyline.
He doesn't look up.
I wave anyway,
one wet second of me, passing.
Could you give me some feedback?

I own a bike shop, and our mechanic Tomasz retires after 25 years. I'm proud of this one: "Tomasz can hear a loose bearing from across the shop and a lie from across the street. He fixed ten thousand flats and handed back every bike like it was new. Tomasz, we're keeping your bench exactly as it is, greasy thumbprints and all. Nobody's allowed to clean it." Thoughts?

Week 10 of my marathon block, aiming for 3:15. Mon: rest, 15 minutes of yoga. Tue: 8x400 m at 5k pace, 90 s jog. Wed: 10 km easy plus 6 strides. Thu: 16 km with 8 km at marathon pace (4:37/km). Fri: rest. Sat: 8 km easy, then 30 minutes of single-leg RDLs and calf raises. Sun: 30 km, last 5 at goal pace. About 85 km total. Would you change anything?

Okay, birders, here's my idea. Lots of us can't describe a song in words, so the app lets you tap the rhythm on the screen and draw the pitch as a rising or falling line. It narrows species by pattern, then plays three candidate recordings to compare. It would also work offline in the field. I'd really like an opinion before I try to prototype it.

Retired court stenographer here, age 71. I've started on a screenplay, and this is my logline: "A 911 dispatcher takes a call from a woman who only whispers about her cat, and has eleven minutes to decode what the cat means before her abuser returns." I'd love an outside opinion, if you don't mind.

I'm a hospice night nurse, 43, and my coworkers encouraged me to write this down: "When a hospice nurse notices her dying patients all ask for the same stranger in their final hour, she tracks him down and finds a lonely locksmith who has never met any of them." Tell me what you think, please.

I own a tiny bookshop and tweeted this today: "A customer wanted 'a book that feels like a rainy Sunday but isn't sad.' I hesitated for four full seconds, which is a long time in bookselling, then handed her Howl's Moving Castle. She's back for the sequel and brought her sister." Thoughts?

Here's my idea: erosion control. I build four 30° slopes in trays: bare soil, grass, mulch, and gravel. A watering can with 100 drilled holes simulates 20 minutes of steady rain from a fixed height. I collect the runoff and dry it to find the sediment mass, and I measure the total water volume too. Three replicates per cover. What do you think?

I'm a high school senior who volunteers as a debate coach, and I'm adding it to my resume for college job applications. Bullet: "Founded and coached a 9-student middle school debate team from scratch; within two seasons, 4 students qualified for the regional tournament." Curious what you make of it!

units: Pastry chef here, testing this for our autumn menu. Pear and rye tart: rye flour pâte sucrée, filled with brown butter frangipane (120g butter, browned and cooled; 120g almond flour; 100g sugar; 2 eggs). Fan thin slices of roasted Bosc pear on top, then glaze with thyme-infused honey and finish with flaky salt. Bake at 175°C for 38 minutes. I'd love an outside opinion before it goes on the menu.

I'm nervous about this one. It's my first design: a 10x10 ft moss garden under a Japanese maple in Portland. A single weathered basalt boulder sits off-centre, with raked gravel flowing around it like a stream. Hair cap moss goes on the shaded side and cushion moss on the sunlit side. A slate stepping path bends once so you can't see the whole garden at a glance. Would you tell me what you think?

I'm a farmer, and I set aside 1 acre on the edge of my property for a wildlife pond and meadow. A 20m x 10m pond with a shallow shelf on the south side, and a deep area of 2.5m on the north. A wildflower meadow, mown only in September, surrounds it, with a hedgerow of hawthorn, blackthorn, and dog rose on the windward side. A log pile and a stone hibernaculum for amphibians sits at the east end. Do you have any feedback?

Hobbyist trying some fine-dining tricks at home. Tomato water: blend 2kg ripe tomatoes with 15g salt, basil stems and a splash of sherry vinegar, then hang in cheesecloth overnight without squeezing. Set 500ml of the clear liquid with 3 gelatin sheets, and serve cold over burrata and charred corn with basil oil. I'm a bit nervous to share this. Any advice?

I'm a linguistics major, and my idea is menu rewrites for immigrant-owned restaurants. Not translation, but descriptions that explain a dish to local diners: 'Injera: a spongy sourdough flatbread you eat with your hands. Yes, it's meant to be shared.' $90 flat, with a printed table card. I did two for free near campus and both owners said customers started asking for the dishes by name. Could this be a real business?

I'm an environmental science grad student. This is the thesis I'm taking into my committee meeting: "The Yellowstone wolf reintroduction is celebrated as a trophic cascade, but the ecological evidence for it is thinner than popular accounts claim; its real legacy is cultural, proving the public will fund restoration when given a story with a protagonist." Thoughts?

I'm a vet, and I want to start a dental plan for pets. $19 a month covers a yearly scaling under anesthesia, a home-brushing kit, and a video call with a tech every quarter to check your technique. I've seen too many dogs lose teeth at eight because the cleaning cost $600 at once. My plan makes that cost small and regular. Be honest, would you sign up your own dog?

Fifty-three, in marketing for 25 years, and updating my resume for the first time in a decade. One bullet: "Rebuilt the email onboarding flow for a B2B SaaS product, A/B testing 14 variants; trial-to-paid conversion rose from 8.2% to 13.5%, adding $1.1M in ARR." Would love to hear what you make of it.

I run a small bakery and wrote this haiku during a 4 a.m. shift:
Flour dusts my wrists—
the oven ticks, half awake,
before the first bird.
Could you tell me what you think of it?

I'm opening a vet clinic called Tailwind. The mark is a dog's tail, side-on, drawn as three nested arcs of decreasing length, each stroke a bit thinner. They read as a wag, but they also read as wind lines. The clinic name sits to the right in lowercase, and the arcs are teal. I'd love a candid reaction before I send it to the printer.

units: I'm a marathon runner, 52, and posted this on Strava after my race: "Mile 22, a kid held a sign: 'Your legs have been lying to you since mile 14.' I laughed so hard I forgot to hurt for almost a minute. 4:12. A personal best at 52. Legs are liars. Be a better liar." Does it read okay to someone who doesn't run? Thanks!

Librarian here, please tell me what you think of my bio: "Things I can find: your lost book, the quietest chair in any building, a good reason to stay in. Things I can't: my keys, a gym habit. I've read two thousand novels and still don't understand people, which is why I'd like to keep studying one. The reference desk is open."

Here's my plan: road salt versus roadside grass. I'll germinate 50 native grass seeds per dish in NaCl solutions of 0, 1, 2, and 4 g/L, four dishes each. I'll count germinated seeds daily for 14 days and graph the curves, not just the final percentage, so delays show up. I also measure radicle length on day 14. Honest feedback welcome, please!

I'm a hospice chaplain, and I've been writing a novel about a family after a death. The first line is: "Grief is mostly logistics, my aunt told me, and then she handed me the casserole dishes and a list of forty-three people to call." I'd be interested in your thoughts.

I'm an undergrad writing my history honours thesis. My question is: "Why did Ottoman port authorities in Salonica begin recording ship cargoes in French in the 1880s, and what does that choice reveal about who the records were meant for?" What's your opinion?

This is the sign I taped to my plant shop door and then photographed for Instagram: "Closed Monday for my daughter's piano recital. She's playing Clair de Lune and has warned me that if I cry, she'll know. The ferns are holding the fort. Back Tuesday, 9am." Any feedback?

Film studies sophomore, and I'm excited about this paper. Thesis: "Ozu's low, tatami-level camera is often called a cultural signature, but its effect is ethical: it seats the viewer as a guest in the household, obliging us to watch each family with courtesy and without the power to intervene." What's your opinion?

I'm 15 and wrote this for English class. Here's my first paragraph:
"On Europa Station, we measure time in oxygen. A birthday is a hundred and ninety thousand breaths; a funeral is however long the rest of us can hold ours. My sister has been dead for four minutes, and I am still counting, because someone has to."
Any feedback?

I own a tiny bookshop and tweeted this today: "A customer wanted 'a book that feels like a rainy Sunday but isn't sad.' I hesitated for four full seconds, which is a long time in bookselling, then handed her Howl's Moving Castle. She's back for the sequel and brought her sister." Thoughts?

My yarn budget is $50/month and I've got rules for it: $30 for yarn for projects already planned and charted, $10 for needles and notions, $5 for my local dyer's club, and $5 wildcard for anything that grabs me. If the wildcard isn't spent it carries over. Do you have any thoughts on it? I'm a little shy about sharing this!

units: PhD in marine ecology here, applying for a science communication role. My opening paragraph: "I spent fourteen months counting the eggs of a snail smaller than a lentil, and I can make you care about it in ninety seconds. Here's how: it's the only thing standing between a kelp forest and an urchin takeover. Everything is somebody's whole world. My job is to show you whose." Feedback welcome!

Hi! I'm 16 and this is the first logline I've written for a film project in my media class: "When her father, a small-town marching band director, slowly loses his hearing, a teenage drum major secretly conducts the band from the field while he believes he's still leading it." Could you tell me what you think?

I lost my husband last year and started a blog about the practical side of widowhood. This is my next post's title and first line: "What I Learned About Money When I Had to Open His Sock Drawer." "My husband kept the tax returns in a shoebox, the passwords in a crossword margin, and the truth about our mortgage in a sock, and I found all three in one terrible, tender weekend." How does it read to you?

I'm a civil engineering technician and I'm planning a mini concrete project for my niece. We'll cast 12 beams (4x4x16 cm) with 0, 1%, 2%, and 3% fibers by volume (hair, straw, or shredded plastic bags). Each beam is supported at both ends, and a bucket on the middle slowly fills with sand until the beam breaks. The failure load is divided by the beam's mass. All beams will cure 28 days. Does this seem like a solid project?

My project compares 3D-printed infill patterns: gyroid, grid, and honeycomb. Each test cube is adjusted to exactly 12.0 g (±0.1) so strength is per unit mass. I print five of each and load them with sand until they fail, recording the mass of sand at the crack. Same filament, same print temperature. Tell me what you think, please. I'm happy to take criticism.

I'm a night-shift nurse, eleven years in, and I've finally started writing. Here's a title and opening line for my first post: "What the Night Shift Knows About Silence." "At 3:40 a.m. the hospital hums in B-flat, and after eleven years I can tell from a change in that hum which floor is about to have a bad hour." I'd really appreciate your feedback.

I'm three weeks into a new job and my manager asked for onboarding feedback. Here's my reply. Does it seem fair and useful?
"Hi Danielle, what's working: shadowing Kofi. What slowed me: I waited six days for system access. I've drafted a day-one checklist (attached) from what I wish I'd had. Happy to be the guinea pig for the next hire."

I have ADHD and get bored by week two, so my plan has fixed anchors and random variety. Mon legs, Tue push, Thu pull, Sat carries and run. Each day's main lift never changes (squat, press, row, farmer carry). Accessories come from rolling a die against a list of six per day. Wed/Fri: 20-minute walk with podcasts. Sun: off. Tracking is one tick on the fridge. Do you think it holds together?

I'm a junior copywriter, and this is my first pitch to a real client, a family-owned hearing-aid clinic. My line: "Hear the kettle again. The rain. Your granddaughter's whisper." Nervous to show it. How does it come across?

Hello! This is my winter-interest border for Minnesota, 10x30 ft along the garage. Red twig dogwood at the back for stem colour against the snow. Mid layer: switchgrass 'Northwind' and sedum 'Matrona', both left standing. A paper birch cluster at the east end with white bark glowing at sunrise. Hellebores are tucked in near the door, so there's something to see on the shortest days. I'd like to know what you think!

I'm an amateur astronomer and posted this on Facebook: "Saturn tonight through my $90 telescope: tiny, tilted, impossible, rings like a hat. My daughter asked if it was a sticker on the lens. I said no. She was quiet for a full minute, which has never happened." Tell me what you think!

I'm opening a cafe that serves coffee by day and natural wine by night. I'd name it "Zenith & Nadir," the highest and lowest points, one for each half of the day. I'd value hearing what you think of it.

I'm 72 and my granddaughter doesn't speak Tagalog. So: in Lola's kitchen there's one rule, you can only ask for something by its name in the other language. The heron holds the river's one idea
so still the water starts to doubt itself.

of a minnow, and the whole grey sentence
resolves into a throat.

units:
Hi, this is the label copy for my first hot sauce. I'm 19 and a bit nervous about showing it to anyone.
"Slow Burn No. 3. Fermented red jalapeños, roasted garlic, a spoon of honey. Starts sweet, goes quiet, then arrives at the back of your throat four seconds later, like a guest who's been parked outside. Good on eggs, better on fried chicken. Medium heat. Shake gently; it has opinions."
Honest thoughts?

I run a small ferry and whale-watching business. Captain Joan retires this weekend, and I'll say: "Joan has crossed this bay nine thousand times and still points at the water like she's never seen it. Tourists come for whales. They stay because she makes them look. Joan, you taught us the sea isn't a show, it's a conversation. Fair winds. Your chair stays at the wheel, facing out." What do you think?

I'm a hospice chaplain, and I've been writing a novel about a family after a death. The first line is: "Grief is mostly logistics, my aunt told me, and then she handed me the casserole dishes and a list of forty-three people to call." I'd be interested in your thoughts.

ok so i wrote a haiku for english class and i kinda want a second opinion before i hand it in
Group chat goes silent—
the typing dots appear, stop,
appear, stop again
thoughts?

I'm a dog groomer and I've been wanting to write for my clients. Title: "Your Dog Is Not Afraid of the Bath." First sentence: "Most dogs I meet aren't afraid of water; they're afraid of slipping, and once you put down a rubber mat, the 'bath-hating' dog you've described for six years quietly disappears." What's your take?

I'm 71 and I knit blankets to sell at the craft fair. My granddaughter told me to ask people online for opinions. This is my tag:
"Merino cot blanket, knitted in honeycomb stitch, which holds warmth without weight. Washed in lanolin so it stays soft. Nine evenings of work. Machine washable on the wool cycle, and made to be handed down: the edges are bound twice, because babies are hard on everything."
Does it work?

I'm 65 and just retired after 40 years as a high school band director. At my party I said: 'Forty years of teenagers, and I've heard every wrong note a human can play. I miss none of them. I miss all of them. Please don't clap on one and three. And if you must cry, do it in tempo.' Casually curious how that works on paper.

I own a small bakery and write on slow afternoons. Here's how my short story opens: "The first thing my grandmother taught me about bread was that it lies. 'Dough tells you it's ready when it isn't,' she'd say, 'and tells you it's ruined when it's only shy.' She died in March. I have fed her starter every day since, though it has never once forgiven me for not being her." Honest thoughts?

I'm a college sophomore starting a laundry fund for students who can't afford the machines. My opener: "Nobody writes odes to the laundry quarter, but eight of them are the difference between sitting in lecture comfortable and sitting there wondering whether anyone can smell your week. We'd like to make that difference free." Opinion?

I'm 16 and run a mowing business with 14 customers. June plan: 14 × 4 visits × $35 = $1,960. Gas $86, trimmer line and blades $30, mower fund $150, flyers $20, tax set-aside 15% ($294), car savings $700, college $380, spending money $300. Zero left over. Mind giving me your honest opinion?

units: No stove in my dorm, only a rice cooker, so here's what I make: ½ cup jasmine rice, 6 cups water, 3 slices ginger and one dried shiitake on the porridge setting. Ladle the boiling congee over a bowl of raw minced scallion, ginger and salt so the heat wilts them. Top with a soft egg, soy, white pepper and chili crisp. Is this a decent recipe? Be honest!

Here's my plan: road salt versus roadside grass. I'll germinate 50 native grass seeds per dish in NaCl solutions of 0, 1, 2, and 4 g/L, four dishes each. I'll count germinated seeds daily for 14 days and graph the curves, not just the final percentage, so delays show up. I also measure radicle length on day 14. Honest feedback welcome, please!

Freelance illustrator, income swings a lot. I budget off my lowest month of the last year, $2,400: rent 900; food 320; health insurance 210; phone/internet 90; software 55; transit 60; personal 125; tax account 640. Anything above that gets split: 30% tax, 40% buffer until I hit three months, 30% to me. Thoughts? Be blunt.

I'm a sci-fi nerd and I run a small comic shop. Here's my movie logline: "A janitor aboard a generation ship discovers that the destination planet was reached two hundred years ago, and the officers have been circling in secret because they like being officers." What do you think?

I'm a tailor, and my book is about trousers. "Hem" follows one pair of corduroys across three brothers. Each page the hem is let down an inch, and the pockets hold what the last boy left: a pebble, a bus ticket, a dried worm. On the final page the youngest hears the jingle and realizes he's wearing his brothers' whole childhoods. Tell me what you think!

I own a flower shop and I'm training for my first marathon (week 10 of 16). Mon: rest. Tue: 8 miles easy. Wed: 6 miles with 3x1 mile at tempo. Thu: 5 easy plus strides, 20 min strength. Fri: rest. Sat: 16 mile long run, last 3 at goal pace. Sun: 4 recovery miles. Wedding season hits in May, so Fridays stay empty on purpose. What's your take?

I ran my first marathon and wrote this on Facebook afterward. Would you read it and tell me what you think? "Mile 20 is where the marathon asks what you actually came for. Mine answered: to show my dad, who can't walk anymore, that the legs he gave me still work. 4:12:09."

I help organize our town's charity 10K as a hobby and I'm using it on my resume for a nonprofit events job. Bullet: "Co-directed a 300-runner charity 10K; secured road closures from two municipalities and raised $22,400 for the children's hospital on a $3,100 budget." Honest opinion please?

I analyze my own online chess games for fun. Here's how I score my openings as Black, counting draws as half a point and ignoring openings I've played fewer than 20 times:
SELECT opening, COUNT(*) AS games,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE result WHEN 'win' THEN 1.0 WHEN 'draw' THEN 0.5 ELSE 0 END), 3) AS score
FROM games
WHERE color = 'black'
GROUP BY opening
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20
ORDER BY score DESC;
What do you reckon?
I'm 10 and I made up a joke for my class talent show. What did the clock say when it got sent to the principal? "I was only tocking." My mum says I should ask someone else. What do you think?

I own a small print shop and needed delivery dates that skip weekends and holidays. This is what I came up with. Thoughts?
```python
from datetime import timedelta
def add_business_days(start, n, holidays=frozenset()):
    step = 1 if n >= 0 else -1
    d = start
    while n:
        d += timedelta(days=step)
        if d.weekday() < 5 and d not in holidays:
            n -= step
    return d
```

```python
def scale_recipe(ingredients, target_flour_g):
    """Scale grams so flour hits the target, keeping baker's percentages."""

```

WITH s AS (
  SELECT user_id,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'view') AS v,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'cart') AS c,
    MIN(ts) FILTER (WHERE step = 'pay') AS p
  FROM funnel_events GROUP BY user_id)
SELECT COUNT(v) AS viewed, COUNT(c) FILTER (WHERE c >= v) AS carted, COUNT(p) FILTER (WHERE p >= c AND c >= v) AS paid FROM s;

units:
I drive long-haul and write on the notes app at truck stops. This one came to me in Nebraska. What's your take?
Nebraska takes an hour to finish a sentence.
The grain elevators raise their one white word
and drop it behind me.
Somewhere past Kearney I say your name
to the windshield, which holds it a mile and lets go.

I run a ten-rod allotment plot and have worked out a four-year rotation. It's divided into four 5x6m blocks: legumes, brassicas, roots, then alliums with potatoes. Between the blocks run 45cm paths that line up with a central compost bay of three bins. Perennials (rhubarb, asparagus, artichokes) sit along the north edge so they never shade anything. Flowers for the bees run along the paths' edges. How does it look to you?

I'm 72 and my granddaughter doesn't speak Tagalog. So: in Lola's kitchen there's one rule, you can only ask for something by its name in the other language. "Pass the salt" becomes "asin," and soon Mari is hungry in two languages. Every page adds a word and a recipe. What's your opinion? Be honest, I've survived worse.

I'm a lifelong birder, and I've designed an app called Quiet List. You record a bird call and it identifies the species and adds it to your life list with a timestamp. For threatened species it saves your location only as a 10 km square, and it never uploads the exact spot. That way nesting sites stay safe, and your data still helps researchers. How does it sound to you?

Philosophy grad student here. Here's my thesis for a seminar paper: "The trolley problem endures not because it reveals our moral intuitions but because it strips away the substance of moral life, relationships of prior obligation, so its answers describe only how people behave toward strangers they will never meet." Where would you push on it?

Okay, birders, here's my idea. Lots of us can't describe a song in words, so the app lets you tap the rhythm on the screen and draw the pitch as a rising or falling line. It narrows species by pattern, then plays three candidate recordings to compare. It would also work offline in the field. I'd really like an opinion before I try to prototype it.

I wrote this chorus for my nana after she passed in March. I'm a sophomore and have never shared a song before, so my hands are a little shaky. Does it work for you?
You measured flour in the hollow of your palm,
salt by the weather, sugar by your mood.
Now I'm guessing in your chipped blue bowl,
and the bread comes out almost you,
and almost is a kind of company, too.

Hi! I'm 16 and this is the first line of my history presentation about my family: "My great-grandmother crossed the Atlantic with one suitcase, a sewing machine, and a lie about her age, and today I want to ask which of those three mattered most." Be honest, what do you think?

I'm a 34-year-old home inspector, and I've been writing a horror screenplay on the side. Here's the logline: "A home inspector notices that every house in a new subdivision has one more room on the inside than on the outside, and the extra rooms are starting to be occupied." Be honest, what's your take?

Proud of this one from my SQL homework! Find students who've completed every required course:
SELECT s.name
FROM students s
JOIN enrollments e ON e.student_id = s.id AND e.completed
JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id AND c.required
GROUP BY s.id, s.name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses WHERE required);
I'd really like your feedback on it.

units:
I own a little flower shop and wrote this on my lunch break. Showing it to you first, before anyone I know:
I can tell which bouquets will be forgiven
by how the man holds them:
like a question,
or like an alibi.
How does it read to you?

I spent twelve years as a paralegal and I'm opening a cafe across from the county courthouse. The name: "Grounds for Appeal." Lawyers and jurors will be my main customers. Does it work for you, or would you change anything?

I sell empanadas from a food truck and I'm writing the market manager. I'm excited but a bit nervous:
"Hi Ms. Lindqvist, I've been at the Saturday market for 14 weeks and sold out by 1 p.m. every time. Could I move from the back lot to the corner near the fountain? The line currently blocks no one, but at the corner I could double the queue space. I'd also add a compostable-packaging pledge. Happy to chat. Warmly, Valentina"

I run a small bakery and wrote this haiku during a 4 a.m. shift:
Flour dusts my wrists—
the oven ticks, half awake,
before the first bird.
Could you tell me what you think of it?

Flattening JSON order items in Postgres. Our orders come from three vendors, so the key isn't always present:
SELECT o.id, item->>'sku' AS sku, (item->>'qty')::int AS qty
FROM orders o
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(o.payload->'items') AS item
WHERE o.payload ? 'items';
Backend dev, 2 years of experience. I'd like your thoughts, especially on whether I'm missing something.

I'm 55 and started saving late, so I'm catching up. Take-home $5,400: mortgage 1,450; groceries 500; utilities 280; car 350; health insurance 400; 401k catch-up 1,000; HSA 300; help with my son's college 500; fun 200; misc 420. Feeling a bit anxious about it. How does this look to you?

I'm a public health officer, and this is the question I'm proposing for our county study: "In rural counties with a single pharmacy, how does closure alter 90-day adherence to antihypertensives, and is the effect mediated by travel distance or by losing a relationship with a pharmacist?" Any thoughts?
I'm a retired sailor who now makes waxed canvas bags. Slogan for the tag: "Carried through worse weather than this." I'd like to hear what you think.

This is the new homepage copy for my plumbing company: "A $20 valve inspection is boring. A flooded kitchen at 2 a.m. is not. Most of our emergency calls started as a drip someone meant to look at. Book a yearly check, and the only exciting thing in your house will be dinner." Does it sound like a real person wrote it?

units:
I run a tiny bakery and I'm rewriting our menu. Here's the entry for our main loaf:
"Country loaf. 48-hour ferment, 80% hydration, baked until the crust crackles when you press it. Sour enough to wake you up, mild enough for a child's lunchbox. Best on day one, toasted on day three, croutons on day five. We bake 40 a morning; when they're gone, they're gone."
What's your opinion?

I've been given the lease on a lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Northumberland coast, and I'm turning it into a cafe. The name is "Last Light." We'll close at dusk, so you can watch the lamp come on while you finish your tea. I'm 62 and a bit sentimental about it. What's your reaction to the name?

I'm a weekend woodworker selling at a craft fair, and this is my sign copy. "End-grain walnut and maple board, 14 x 10 inches. Knife edges sink between the fibers and the grain closes behind them, so your blades stay sharper and the board shows fewer scars. Finished with mineral oil and beeswax. About six pounds, heavy enough to stay put while you chop." Any thoughts?

I'm a 911 dispatcher, 48. Here's what I said at Carla's last-shift party: 'Carla has been the first voice on the worst day of ten thousand lives. She never got to see how any of them ended. She just said, "Stay on the line with me," and they did. Tonight, Carla, we're the ones saying it. Stay on the line. Visit. Bring the good cookies.' Nervous to share. Thoughts?

I taught fourth grade for 34 years and I'm applying to be a docent at the natural history museum. This is my paragraph: "Every September I handed my students a whale vertebra I'd bought at a yard sale and said nothing for a full minute. The questions they asked in that silence taught me more about teaching than any training did. I'd like to bring that minute of silence to your visitors." Could you tell me what you make of it?

I'm a second-year econ PhD student trying to write for a general audience. Title: "The Bus Fare Is a Lie We Agreed On." Opening: "Every city bus fare is a price set not by what a ride costs but by what a mayor can survive charging, which makes the fare box less a cash register than a weekly opinion poll." Does it work for you?

I teach piano in a rural village and I'm making a logo for my studio, called Flock Music. Five staff lines roll like green hills. Perched on the lines as notes are little sheep: a round woolly body for the note head and a thin stem upward for the tail. One black sheep is a note in the middle. What do you think of the idea?

I'm a documentary filmmaker pitching to funders next month. My pitch begins: "For forty years, Ruth Alvarez recorded the weather every morning at 6 a.m. in a notebook, and in all that time nobody asked her why. I did, and the answer is not about weather." Could I get your honest reaction?

I supervise a warehouse and I'm not much of a writer. This is going to my manager. Any thoughts?
"Karen, Bay 4's forklift aisle is 2.1m wide; the new pallets need 2.4. Two near-misses this month, photos attached. Options: move the racking (about a day, no cost) or make the aisle one-way. I'd move the racking; I can do it Saturday with two people. Need your OK by Thursday."

made a card game w my friends and wrote the back-of-box blurb
"Heist Night. 3–6 players. You're a crew of thieves robbing a museum, and one of you is secretly the informant. Play cards to crack the vault, or quietly sabotage it. 20 minutes, no board, one very suspicious silence. Trust is a resource. Spend wisely."
what do u think??

units:
I'm a hobbyist drone photographer and want to pitch a hotel manager. Here's the email:
"Dear Ms. Aoki, I'm a local photographer, and last week at golden hour I shot your hotel's rooftop terrace from above, attached. The frame shows the pool, the hills behind, and the sunset hitting the cabanas. I'd be glad to shoot a full set of ten images for your website for $250. I'm licensed to fly in this area. May I send a quote? Regards, Daniel"
What do you think?

I drive long-haul and write on my phone at truck stops. Just finished the start of a blog post, "Weigh Station Poetry." It goes: "Between Amarillo and nowhere, the CB starts to sound like a congregation, forty strangers trading weather and warnings in a language none of us admitted we were inventing." Tell me what you make of it?

I'm 68 and retired, and I'm sick of mosquito-repelling phone apps. For my grandson's fair, we'll build a two-chamber choice box with a screen divider, put in 20 fruit flies, and then play the app's tone on only one side. A blinded helper chooses the side with a coin flip. After 10 minutes we count the flies per side. Then we'll repeat it 30 times and run a binomial test. What's your opinion?

Hi! I'm 16 and I made these for my family's New Year dinner and I'm kind of nervous about sharing. Black sesame shortbread: 200g butter, 90g powdered sugar, 250g flour, 40g toasted ground black sesame, 1 tbsp orange zest, ½ tsp salt. Chill the dough 1 hour, slice, then roll the edges in raw sesame seeds. Bake at 160°C for 22 minutes. Could you tell me what you think?

We're farmers and just started jarring pickles. My wife says I should ask strangers what they think. Here's the label text:
"Dill spears from our back field, picked at breakfast, jarred by lunch. Garlic, dill heads, sea salt, and a grape leaf to keep them crunchy. No sugar, no vinegar, just a warm week on the counter. Open one on a hot day. Once opened, they keep two months in the fridge, though they rarely last a week."

I'm a medical interpreter and need to update my resume. Here's the bullet I'm working with: "Interpreted live for 300+ oncology consults in Mandarin and Cantonese; led creation of an 85-term bilingual glossary now used by the hospital's entire language services department." Does it work for you?

Soup dumplings from scratch, my weekend project. Filling: 500g pork with 30% fat, ginger-scallion water added in three batches and stirred in one direction, then 300g cold pork-skin aspic, cubed and folded in. Wrappers: hot-water dough, rolled thin at the edges and thicker in the centre, 18 pleats. Steam 8 minutes on cabbage leaves. What would you improve?

Nursing student here, about to put this on my profile. Can you tell me what you think?
Good at: finding a vein first try, parallel parking, remembering your dog's name.
Working on: sourdough, leaving the group chat on read, believing me when I say "I'm fine."
Night rotations mean my weekends are Tuesdays. If you can be cheerful about dinner at 8 a.m., we'll get along.

ok so my mate dared me to write something funny. Opening of my story:
"Gary Pemberton-Voss had been a respectable supervillain for eleven years when his henchmen unionised. units:
I wrote this chorus for my nana after she passed in March. I'm a sophomore and have never shared a song before, so my hands are a little shaky. Does it work for you?
You measured flour in the hollow of your palm,
salt by the weather, sugar by your mood.
Now I'm guessing in your chipped blue bowl,
and the bread comes out almost you,
and almost is a kind of company, too.

I'm a bike mechanic, and I want to open a repair cart outside the train station. You drop your bike at 8 a.m. with a tag that lists the issues, and I text you a quote before 9. If you reply "yes," it's done by 5:30, and you pick it up on your way home. If you reply "no," it's free of charge to wait. No shop rent, just a cart and a trailer. What do you think about this idea?

I translate Korean webtoons as a fan hobby, and I'm applying for a junior localization job. This is my cover letter paragraph on translation philosophy. What do you make of it?
"In one series, a character says '밥 먹었어?' to mean 'I love you.' A literal translation says 'Did you eat?' A faithful one says something else entirely. I've learned to keep the question and add the worry around it: 'Have you eaten yet? You look tired.'"

I've been home with my kids for 8 years and I'm applying for a project coordinator job. Nervous! Paragraph: "For eight years I've managed a team of three with unpredictable deadlines, no budget, and a 6 a.m. launch every day. I also ran the school auction, which raised $41,000 using one spreadsheet and fifty unreliable volunteers. People call that a transferable skill. I'd like to prove it on yours." Honest reaction, please?

I'm a line cook who got curious about browning. I'll caramelize identical onion slices in solutions of baking soda at five different pH levels, then photograph each batch every 5 minutes next to a gray card and convert the pixels to L*a*b* color values. Then I'll plot how fast browning happens against pH. I'm a little nervous presenting at a science fair as a non-scientist. What do you think of it?

I'm a nursing student and wrote this for my evidence-based practice course. "Among night-shift med-surg nurses, does a protected 20-minute nap at 3 a.m. reduce medication-administration near-misses in the final three hours of the shift, compared with no scheduled break?" Could you give me your honest opinion? I'm a little nervous about it.
I'm a linguist turned app founder. Our language-learning app's slogan is: "Be the one who orders for the table." Could you give me your thoughts on it?

For my education course I wrote "Tuesday Is Late." Leo waits at the front door for Tuesday, because Mum said it was coming. Through the day the postman arrives, then rain, then Grandma with a bag of oranges. By dinner Leo decides Tuesday is made of all of them. I'm a bit worried about it being too quiet for a read-aloud. Can you give me your honest take?

I'm 40 and a T10 paraplegic. I want to build strength without wrecking my shoulders. Mon: seated cable rows 4x10, face pulls 3x15, landmine press 3x8. Tue: handcycle intervals, 6x2 min hard/2 easy. Wed: rest. Thu: lat pulldowns 4x8, parallel-bar dips 3x6, rotator cuff band work. Fri: 30-minute steady handcycle. Sat: Pallof presses and core. Sun: rest. Pulling volume is double pushing on purpose. Thoughts?

I'm 12 and this is my opening for our debate club. The motion is that homework should be abolished. Can you give me feedback? "My opponent says homework builds discipline. Fine. If discipline is the goal, let's assign something honest: wash a dish, call a grandparent, wait in a queue without a phone. Those have never once been marked down for neatness."

units: This is the sign I taped to my plant shop door and then photographed for Instagram: "Closed Monday for my daughter's piano recital. She's playing Clair de Lune and has warned me that if I cry, she'll know. The ferns are holding the fort. Back Tuesday, 9am." Any feedback?

Pareto analysis for our catalogue: what share of revenue the top products make. I added the tie-breaker and ROWS frame deliberately.
WITH r AS (SELECT product_id, SUM(revenue) AS rev FROM sales GROUP BY product_id)
SELECT product_id, rev,
  SUM(rev) OVER (ORDER BY rev DESC, product_id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) / SUM(rev) OVER () AS cum_share
FROM r ORDER BY rev DESC, product_id;
I'm a finance manager, not a developer. Does this look right to you?

Hey, I coach distance runners and write a small newsletter. Next post is titled "Mile 20 Is a Negotiation." I open with: "Nobody warns you that at mile twenty your body will open with a lowball offer, and the whole skill of the sport is knowing it's only the first one." Could you tell me how this reads to you?

I'm a 1600-rated club chess player writing up a project for fun. My question: "For players rated 1400 to 1800 in 15+10 online games, do time-trouble blunders cost more rating points than opening errors, and does that balance shift after a player's first thirty games?" I'd use Lichess data. Would love any opinion you have!

I'm a tailor with a 12-year-old shop. New service: 'Bought It, Fit It.' People order clothes online and ship them straight to me. After one measurement video call, I alter and send them on for a flat $35. My notes stay on file, so future orders get fixed before they even arrive. I think it turns returns into repeat customers. What do you think?

I illustrate on commission from my home studio and I'm pitching a children's book publisher. Here's the paragraph from my letter, wondering what you think.
"I draw the sort of picture a child finds on the third reading: the mouse behind the curtain, the half-eaten pear under the bed, the cat who looks guilty in every scene. My sketchbooks are full of these small secrets, and I would like to hide them in your books."

I'm a dog groomer and I've been wanting to write for my clients. Title: "Your Dog Is Not Afraid of the Bath." First sentence: "Most dogs I meet aren't afraid of water; they're afraid of slipping, and once you put down a rubber mat, the 'bath-hating' dog you've described for six years quietly disappears." What's your take?

Hi! For my databases course I had to list every consecutive-day login streak per user. Here's my Postgres attempt:
WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, login_at::date AS d FROM logins),
g AS (SELECT user_id, d, d - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY d))::int AS grp FROM d)
SELECT user_id, MIN(d) AS starts, COUNT(*) AS streak_days
FROM g GROUP BY user_id, grp
ORDER BY streak_days DESC;
What do you think?

Ex-army, best man, and deadpan by nature. Draft: "I've served with Pete in two countries and one wedding rehearsal. Only the rehearsal made him sweat. Dani, I've watched this man wade into a flooded river to rescue a stranger's bag, and I've watched him cry at a dog food advert. He is brave for the right reasons and soft for the best ones. Look after both." How's the tone?

I'm a 26-year-old teacher in Leeds. Take-home £2,100: rent £780; council tax £95; bills £110; groceries £230; train £70; phone £18; Lifetime ISA £250 (for the 25% bonus); student loan overpay £120; fun £150; gifts £40; holiday pot £137; buffer £100. I'd love to know what you think, honestly.

units: I own a laundromat, and last month I added an espresso bar in the front corner. I'm calling the whole place "Delicates." The sign would be hand-painted, cold-water-wash-label style. Curious what you make of it!

I run a used bookshop and wrote a jazzy little number about it. Here's the chorus. I'd be curious about your reaction, whatever it is.
Every book on this shelf was somebody's Tuesday night,
a train ride, a bathtub, a borrowed flashlight.
I just keep the kettle on and the lamp lit low,
and the dead keep writing to whoever's up.

I'm 15 and wrote this for English class. Here's my first paragraph:
"On Europa Station, we measure time in oxygen. A birthday is a hundred and ninety thousand breaths; a funeral is however long the rest of us can hold ours. My sister has been dead for four minutes, and I am still counting, because someone has to."
Any feedback?

I'm a software engineer and I've planned a 5m x 7m garden inspired by Japanese design, but adapted to Ohio. The idea: three clustered stones in an area of raked gravel, shaped like a dry stream. It's crossed by a flat stone bridge. A Japanese maple stands in the corner, and I've placed moss under a shaded eave. I'm keeping the plant list to nine species, and nothing is symmetrical. Here's the plan. What do you think?

Hello! This is my winter-interest border for Minnesota, 10x30 ft along the garage. Red twig dogwood at the back for stem colour against the snow. Mid layer: switchgrass 'Northwind' and sedum 'Matrona', both left standing. A paper birch cluster at the east end with white bark glowing at sunrise. Hellebores are tucked in near the door, so there's something to see on the shortest days. I'd like to know what you think!

I've been a newspaper copy editor for thirty years and I'm trying screenwriting. Logline: "Two obituary writers at a dying small-town paper, long at war over each other's prose, each begin secretly writing the other's obituary, the most honest work either has done in years." What do you make of it?

This is my first draft for an industrial design class assignment. "Halo Clip is a rear bike light that wraps around the seatpost and glows in a full ring, so drivers see you from the side as well as behind. USB-C charging, 12-hour runtime, and a silicone band that fits any post from 25 to 35 mm. At 41 grams, it weighs less than two AA batteries." Thoughts?

I've been given the lease on a lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Northumberland coast, and I'm turning it into a cafe. The name is "Last Light." We'll close at dusk, so you can watch the lamp come on while you finish your tea. I'm 62 and a bit sentimental about it. What's your reaction to the name?

I'm a retired ferry captain turning a moored barge into a floating cafe. I'm naming it "Dead Reckoning," the old way of finding your position without landmarks, and now it's how I find my way into retirement. How does it strike you?

units: Thesis paragraph from my philosophy paper: "Nozick assumes we refuse the experience machine because we want contact with reality. I think we refuse because we want to be answerable: to be the kind of person who can let someone down. A simulated life contains no one we can fail, and so no one whose forgiveness we can earn. That, not the missing real world, is what we'd mourn." Does the argument hold together?

Hi! I'm 16 and I made these for my family's New Year dinner and I'm kind of nervous about sharing. Black sesame shortbread: 200g butter, 90g powdered sugar, 250g flour, 40g toasted ground black sesame, 1 tbsp orange zest, ½ tsp salt. Chill the dough 1 hour, slice, then roll the edges in raw sesame seeds. Bake at 160°C for 22 minutes. Could you tell me what you think?

I'm a ham radio hobbyist applying to be a 911 dispatcher. Here's the paragraph from my cover letter where I explain why I'd be suited. What's your opinion?
"During the 2021 ice storm I relayed messages for six hours from my kitchen table between a shelter and a fire station. What I remember is how quiet I got. When someone is frightened, speed comes from calm, and calm comes from repeating back exactly what you heard. I'd bring that habit to your center."

I do funeral photography and I'm starting a dark comedy. Logline: "A professional mourner who attends the funerals of the friendless finds herself at her estranged father's service, where no one else has shown up and her professional standards are on the line." Curious what you think!
I'm a dog walker and I'm putting together business cards. The slogan I wrote is "Tired dogs, happy couches." Can you tell me what you think? I'm a bit nervous about showing it to anyone.

I came to the UK ten years ago and posted this on Facebook today: "Ten years ago I arrived in Leeds with two suitcases and one English word: sorry. Today I fixed the boiler of the woman at the bus stop who taught me the second: thanks. She paid in scones. I accept this as legal tender." English is my second language, so I'd love your opinion on how it reads.

I run a small bakery and posted this on Instagram this morning: "Our starter is eleven years old. It has outlasted two ovens, a business partner and one landlord's patience. Loaves out at 7am, and the dark-crust ones go first. Bring a bag." What do you think?

My project compares 3D-printed infill patterns: gyroid, grid, and honeycomb. Each test cube is adjusted to exactly 12.0 g (±0.1) so strength is per unit mass. I print five of each and load them with sand until they fail, recording the mass of sand at the crack. Same filament, same print temperature. Tell me what you think, please. I'm happy to take criticism.

I coordinate a women's shelter and this is the opening of our winter appeal: "Dear friend, The first thing most women ask for when they arrive isn't food or a bed. It's a key, to a door that locks from the inside. We have eight keys. Last year we turned away sixty-three women." I'd really value your opinion before I send it.

I'm a fire captain, not a writer, and I said this for Lou, retiring after 30 years: 'Lou taught me the most important rule of the job: you can be the bravest person in the building, but you still wash your own dishes. Thirty years, he never left a pot in the sink. Thirty years, he never left a person in a fire. I think that's the same habit.' Does it work?

PhD in marine ecology here, applying for a science communication role. My opening paragraph: "I spent fourteen months counting the eggs of a snail smaller than a lentil, and I can make you care about it in ninety seconds. Here's how: it's the only thing standing between a kelp forest and an urchin takeover. Everything is somebody's whole world. My job is to show you whose." Feedback welcome!

Monthly cohort retention for our subscription app. I'm a data scientist and wrote it in one sitting, so tell me if I've missed something.
WITH f AS (
  SELECT customer_id, MIN(date_trunc('month', ordered_at)) AS cohort
  FROM orders GROUP BY 1)
SELECT f.cohort,
  DATEDIFF('month', f.cohort, date_trunc('month', o.ordered_at)) AS months_since,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS active
FROM f JOIN orders o USING (customer_id)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2;

my breath and the elk's breath hang
in the same cold air
What's your opinion of it?

I'm a farmer, new to writing. In the town of Marl, your umbrella opens onto whatever you're feeling: Grandpa's makes drizzle, the mayor's makes hail. Sorry if this is a bit odd. I work in a post office sorting room and this came to me on shift. The start of my story:
"The dead letter office in Perth received, in 1962, a parcel containing forty-one left shoes. No note, no sender. Winifred Ames, who had spent nineteen years reuniting strangers with their mistakes, laid them in a row on the sorting table and felt, for the first time, outmatched."
What's your take?

My loaf: 500g bread flour, 100g whole wheat, 20g toasted barley flour, with cold roasted barley tea replacing the water (80% hydration). 20% levain, four stretch-and-folds, overnight cold proof, baked covered at 245°C for 20 minutes, then uncovered for 22. How does it read to you?
