units: Hi! For my landscape studio course I designed a 12x20 ft Tucson courtyard. One desert willow in the northwest corner shades the hot afternoon wall. A dry-wash path of granite fines curves through brittlebush, Parry's penstemon and a single blue agave. A rain chain empties into a sunken basin planted with sedges. Seating sits on the east side for cool mornings. No turf. I present Thursday, so what's your take?

Here's my bio for a climbing-gym meetup app. I'm a hobbyist climber, nothing fancy. Does it work?
"I'm a 5.10 climber with a 5.13 vocabulary for complaining about it. Strong opinions: chalk bags should be washed, belay attention should be absolute, and the best part of any route is the sitting-down afterward. Looking for a partner who'll catch my falls and my terrible puns, in that order."

I own a small print shop and needed delivery dates that skip weekends and holidays. This is what I came up with. Thoughts?
```python
from datetime import timedelta
def add_business_days(start, n, holidays=frozenset()):
    step = 1 if n >= 0 else -1
    d = start
    while n:
        d += timedelta(days=step)
        if d.weekday() < 5 and d not in holidays:
            n -= step
    return d
```

First-gen student here. I wrote this hook after an internship interview and I'm kind of nervous to show anyone. What's your honest take?
Mama dusted the boardroom where I'm interviewing now,
she knew the table's every scar and never knew how
to ask for a seat there. So I'll sit, and I'll stay,
with her name in my mouth like the first thing I say.

I design board games as a hobby and I'm giving a talk at a small convention. I'm opening with: "The most important rule in my game is on the back of the box, in small type: 'The player who is winning may not know it.'" What's your opinion?

Hey! I run a bakery and wrote a story for the kids who come in on Saturdays. Gerald, a sourdough starter, sulks when he's fed late, and six-year-old Pia learns to read his bubbles like moods. On the last page she tells him she'll be late on Monday, and apologizes first. Any thoughts? I'm mostly curious how it would work read aloud.

I'm a vet tech and my colleagues keep telling me to write down the stuff I say. This one came up on Tuesday: "Every vet knows the animal is rarely the one who needs sedating." I'd love to hear what someone outside the clinic thinks.

I have ADHD and get bored by week two, so my plan has fixed anchors and random variety. Mon legs, Tue push, Thu pull, Sat carries and run. Each day's main lift never changes (squat, press, row, farmer carry). Accessories come from rolling a die against a list of six per day. Wed/Fri: 20-minute walk with podcasts. Sun: off. Tracking is one tick on the fridge. Do you think it holds together?

Tonight I'm opening our astronomy club's star party. Here's the speech: "The light you'll see in Andromeda left 2.5 million years ago, before anything we'd call human. It has been traveling toward this field, this telescope, this paper cup of cocoa in your hand. Please don't rush. It's waited a long time for you. Red flashlights only, and be kind to the dark." What do you reckon?

Bootcamp student here. I needed to turn nested config into flat keys and ended up with this recursive version. How would you rate it?
```js
const flat = (o, p = '') =>
  Object.entries(o).flatMap(([k, v]) =>
    v && typeof v === 'object' ? flat(v, p + k + '.') : [[p + k, v]]);
Object.fromEntries(flat({ a: { b: 1, c: { d: 2 } } }));
```

units: I keep bees, and I sell honey at the farmers' market, so I mapped a forage plan for my 1-acre lot. A six-foot hedge of serviceberry and pussy willow sits in front of the hives to force a high flight path. Bloom runs in order: willow in March, crocus, then lilac, then basswood, then borage and buckwheat in July. Asters and goldenrod go in for autumn. A shallow water dish with pebbles sits 10 ft from the hives. Does it look sensible?

I'm a locksmith with a small business, and my daughter talked me into blogging. Title: "Locked Out at 2 a.m.: A Locksmith's Field Guide to Humility." First sentence: "Nobody calls me because they're having a good night, so the first thing I do on every job is say something small and kind, because the door is the easy part." What do you make of it?

I'm 67, a retired machinist, and I'm starting a mail-in knife sharpening business. My pitch card says: "Send us your dull knife. We'll send you a sharp loaner the same day, so dinner never waits. Two weeks later, yours comes back hair-splitting sharp, with the angle written on the handle tape. $12 a knife. Return shipping is on us." Be straight with me, what do you make of it?

I run a small flower farm and I'm speaking to a florists' association. This is how I want to begin: "A rose on your table has usually travelled eight thousand miles to get there. Tonight I'd like to introduce you to the ones that haven't." Could you give me your honest reaction?

Hi! I'm a pastry chef and I've been writing posts for my bakery's site. New one is called "Why Your Croissants Taste Like Bread With Ambitions." It opens: "Butter doesn't melt at 32°C so much as give up, and the exact moment it does is the whole reason your lamination collapses." Thoughts?

Food truck owner here, and this is my salsa macha: toast 1 cup peanuts, 3 tbsp sesame seeds, and 6 chiles de árbol and 4 guajillos in 1 cup of neutral oil on low until fragrant and just darkening. Cool, then add 4 cloves roasted garlic, 1 tbsp piloncillo, 1 tsp dried orange peel, 1 tbsp cider vinegar and salt. Pulse it chunky. It goes on everything. Thoughts?

Hi! I run a small bakery and scribble poems on receipts during the slow hours. This is the latest:
At four a.m. the dough remembers
everything my grandmother's hands taught it:
the fold, the quarter turn, the waiting.
I only lend it my arms.
By six, the whole street smells of her.
Honest thoughts welcome!

I've been running tabletop RPG campaigns for friends for years and I'm trying to break into game design. Here's my resume bullet: "Designed and ran a 3-year campaign for 7 players; rewrote the combat system after playtests showed fights averaging 94 minutes, cutting them to 35 while preserving player choice." Any feedback?

I'm a development associate at a food bank applying for a director role. This is the bullet I'm sharing in my cover letter too: "Secured $480K in first-time foundation grants by pitching 23 funders; raised donor retention from 38% to 54% by personally calling every donor who gave over $100." How does it land for you?

Student cooking for my flatmates. My cacio e pepe variation: toast black pepper and 1 tsp red Sichuan peppercorns, crush coarsely. Cook 100g tonnarelli in very little water so the starch stays high, and pull it 2 minutes early. Off the heat, mix Pecorino with pasta water into a paste first, then toss everything together with the pepper. Can you give me feedback on the technique?

units: Software engineer here, posted this on Mastodon after a brutal week: "Spent six hours on a 'random' crash. It only happened on Tuesdays. A cached intermediate cert expired at midnight UTC, seven days after each Tuesday deploy. The bug wasn't in the code. It was in the calendar. 'Random' just means you haven't found the clock yet." Would non-engineers get it? Curious what you think.

I'm an amateur astronomer, and my brother asked me for a toast. "When you look at a star, you're seeing light that left it long ago. Some of those stars are gone by the time you notice them. I think of that when I look at Hana and Theo, because what I see tonight, two people lit from inside, started years ago, in a lab hallway, over a broken coffee machine. Keep shining across the distance. To Hana and Theo." Does that read as natural?

I'm a night-shift nurse and cook when I'm exhausted, so this is a one-pot dinner. Toast 2 tsp cumin seeds in olive oil, add onion, garlic, then 1½ cups red lentils and 6 cups water. Simmer 20 minutes. Stir in the chopped rind of half a preserved lemon, finish with lots of black pepper and a spoon of yogurt. Chili butter on top. Does this sound like something worth making again?

I'm 11 and my idea for an app is called Pet Shift. My family has one dog and four people, and he keeps getting fed twice. You tap "Fed Biscuit" once. If someone else tries to tap it within two hours, the phone says "Dad already fed Biscuit 12 minutes ago." Then it shows a picture of Biscuit looking guilty. What do you think? My mom said to ask someone who knows apps.

I keep bees, and I hate pulling off my gloves to take notes. My app is Hive Voice. During an inspection I say "Hive 4, queen seen, eggs yes, six frames of brood, a little crowded," and it fills in a structured log. It flags anything missing, like "No mention of mites." It also compares the entry with last month's. Is this something you could see helping people?

I've kept bees for six years and here's my line for the club talk: "A hive is a company of 40,000 where the CEO never leaves the building, the staff work themselves to death by August, and the men are all fired in autumn." What do you think, too dark?

I'm opening a chess café named En Passant. The logo is a pawn in solid black, front-on. But its round head is a coffee cup seen from above: a ring, dark liquid inside, and a small handle at the right side where a pawn would have nothing. Everything else is perfectly standard. I'd like your opinion, please.

I run a food truck (Korean-Mexican, mostly kimchi quesadillas) and wrote my profile in the same spirit. How's it land?
"I feed strangers from a window for twelve hours a day, so I'm excellent at small talk and terrible at days off. Looking for someone to sit on my truck's tailgate at midnight and tell me what I should put on the specials board. I'll pay in quesadillas. Vegetarian options available. I'm not heartless."

I'm a fire captain, not a writer, and I said this for Lou, retiring after 30 years: 'Lou taught me the most important rule of the job: you can be the bravest person in the building, but you still wash your own dishes. Thirty years, he never left a pot in the sink. Thirty years, he never left a person in a fire. I think that's the same habit.' Does it work?

Proud to finally share this. I'm a Mumbai-based sound editor, 52, and it's the first story I've written myself: "In 1950s Bombay, the unseen playback singer behind a film star's voice must decide whether to expose her when the star's husband falls in love with the voice and not the woman." How does it strike you?

I'm 55 and started saving late, so I'm catching up. Take-home $5,400: mortgage 1,450; groceries 500; utilities 280; car 350; health insurance 400; 401k catch-up 1,000; HSA 300; help with my son's college 500; fun 200; misc 420. Feeling a bit anxious about it. How does this look to you?

Hobbyist beekeeper here. Our club's oldest member, Arlo, is hanging up his veil. My toast: "Arlo told me bees don't care about your day. Move slow, breathe, and they'll let you in. I've tried to live that way since. Sixty years, millions of bees, and only eleven stings, he claims. Arlo, you kept the hives and the humans calm. We'll leave the smoker lit for you." Do you think it works?

I keep aquariums, and I'm trying duckweed as a nitrate sensor. I'll grow 10 fronds per jar in 0, 5, 20, and 50 ppm nitrate, then photograph from above every day for 12 days. ImageJ gives me the green area, which I'll use to calculate the growth rate. Three replicates, same light and temperature. Could I get your opinion on it?

Birding hobbyist here. I put this on Facebook yesterday: "5:42am, Marsden Reedbed. The bittern stood so still I spent ten minutes admiring a reed. Then the reed blinked. Lifer #212, and I forgot to breathe for most of it." Curious how it reads to someone outside the birding world?

Retired DBA here, tinkering for fun. I wrote an org chart query for our club's volunteer table. Cycle guard included, since people enter data badly:
WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (
  SELECT id, name, manager_id, name::text AS path, 0 AS depth FROM staff WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.id, e.name, e.manager_id, c.path || ' > ' || e.name, c.depth + 1
  FROM staff e JOIN chain c ON e.manager_id = c.id WHERE c.depth < 12)
SELECT * FROM chain ORDER BY path;
What's your opinion?

I run a true-crime podcast as a hobby and wrote an essay about the genre. Thesis: "True-crime podcasts promise justice but deliver intimacy: the genre's appeal lies less in solving cases than in the feeling of being trusted with a stranger's worst day, one episode at a time." What do you think?

I teach Spanish at a high school and I'm writing a magical realism novel. First line: "In Villa Seca it rained only on people who were about to lie, which made the elections very short and the weddings very wet." Would love your feedback on it.

Our knitting group has two speeds: "I'll finish it by Christmas" and "Which Christmas?" I said that at last week's meetup and got a laugh, but I'm wondering whether it holds up written down. What do you think, any tweaks?

"Hi Greta, over July 4th weekend, I'd like to reserve five overflow kennels for my regular clients. All five dogs are vaccinated, and I'll send their records by Friday. I'll drop off, feed, and walk them myself, so there's no extra work for your staff. I can pay $200 up front. Could you confirm by the 20th? Thanks, Marcus"
What do you think?

I own a small dumpling restaurant and I'm writing about my mum for the website. Title: "How to Fold a Dumpling Like My Mother Without Her Hands." First line: "My mother's hands folded eighteen pleats without looking, and after her stroke I had to learn to describe in words what her fingers had never needed to say." I'd be grateful to hear what you think.

Long-time fantasy reader, first-time writer here. My novel begins: "Tuesday was the day Thornwick hid its children, so the dragon's tax collector found only goats, a very old man, and an unusually loud silence." Would you tell me what you think? Be gentle, I'm a bit anxious about this.

I'm a hobbyist game designer. Memory-care homes seem to run on bingo, so I made a kit: large tiles with photos of 1950s kitchen objects that residents match and talk about, plus a facilitator card with three open questions. $65 per kit. One activity director tried it, and residents were still chatting after 40 minutes. I'd like to sell it to care homes. What's your take?

Weekend gardener here, and my zucchini has gotten completely out of hand. I turned it into a country chorus. Be straight with me, what's your take?
Zucchini in July, please, I'm begging you stop,
I've left bags on porches, I've filled the church shop.
The neighbors all wave with a too-careful smile.
They've seen me coming up the drive for a mile.

I'm a bassist who's been touring for ten years and this has happened to me twice. "When a band's player gets sick the night before a gig, we get a vetted session musician who has already studied their charts and setlist into the van within twelve hours." What do you think?

I've kept a sourdough starter for four years and decided to write about it. Thesis: "Pandemic sourdough was less a food trend than a time trend: a starter demands feeding on a schedule, and people locked at home wanted something that made the days measurably pass." Any reactions?

I'm a high school junior and wrote this for a film club pitch night. "When a stroke leaves her grandfather speaking only the Cantonese he spent fifty years hiding, a sixteen-year-old who never learned it has one summer to decode his confession." How would you react to this as a pitch?

I own a small bakery and write on slow afternoons. Here's how my short story opens: "The first thing my grandmother taught me about bread was that it lies. 'Dough tells you it's ready when it isn't,' she'd say, 'and tells you it's ruined when it's only shy.' She died in March. I have fed her starter every day since, though it has never once forgiven me for not being her." Honest thoughts?

units: I'm a nursing student and I blog about clinicals. Here's my latest title and first sentence: "What the Night Shift Taught Me Before I Had a License." "At 3 a.m. on my first rotation, a patient who hadn't spoken all week asked me to open the window, and I understood that half of nursing is noticing what people can't bring themselves to request." Thoughts? Anything you'd change?

I've kept bees for six winters and finally tried to capture the sound in a haiku:
January hive—
I press my ear to the wood
and hear them, still there
What's your take? I'm especially unsure how the last line is read by someone outside beekeeping.

I'm a 29-year-old climber working toward my first 8a. Mon: 4 max hangs on a 20mm edge (10 s, +5 kg), then limit bouldering. Tue: 40-minute zone-2 bike, core. Wed: rest. Thu: 4x4s on routes two grades below my limit. Fri: push-ups, reverse wrist curls, shoulder external rotation. Sat: project attempts while fresh. Sun: rest. Every fourth week I halve the volume. How does it look to you?

I'm a financial adviser and I'm speaking to a room of twenty-somethings. I begin: "Imagine a stranger who will inherit everything you earn this year, and who currently receives none of it. He's you, at sixty-seven." How would you react to that if you were sitting in the audience?

I'm 15 and I'm entering a science fair with a bioplastic I made. My intro is: "This is a bag made from last Sunday's potato peels. In six weeks it will be soil, which is more than the bag it replaces can promise in six hundred years." What do you think?

I'm a backend developer applying to a food bank's tech team, taking a pay cut to do it. Cover letter paragraph: "Last year I rewrote our checkout retry logic and saved my company an estimated $2M. This year I'd like to spend my skills on a problem where success is a Tuesday pantry line that moves twelve minutes faster. Your volunteer scheduler has a race condition. I found it in ten minutes and would love to fix it." How does it land?

Hobby beekeeper here, and I'm a little proud of this one. I'd lease rooftop hives to restaurants for $85 a month. I handle all inspections, and they get 20 jars a year labelled with their street name, plus a QR code to a short video of 'their' bees. Chefs get a menu story, and I fund my other 12 hives. Three owners have said they're interested. Does it seem worth pursuing?

Hi! I'm a nurse with 12 years in, updating my resume for a unit manager role. Here's my top bullet: "Cut central-line infection rate on a 28-bed cardiac step-down unit from 4.1 to 0.7 per 1,000 line-days in 14 months by redesigning the dressing-change checklist with night-shift staff and training 63 nurses." Can you give me your honest opinion?

Hey! I'm a freshman and this is my first haiku since middle school. Wrote it walking to class this morning. Any thoughts?
First snow on campus—
the whole quad forgets its paths
until we make them.

I'm a senior engineer, and I'm giving our team's postmortem talk at a dev conference. Opening line: "At 3:07 on a Tuesday morning, we deleted our own database. This talk is about the forty-one minutes in which seven people were kind to each other, which is why we're still in business." Thoughts?

units: I'm a school librarian and an immigrant, and I wrote this one for me too. Linh collects the wrong ways people say her name in jars: Lin, Lynn, Lean. Her grandmother says each jar is a small gift from someone who tried. On the last page, a new teacher asks Linh to say it first. I'd love your thoughts, truly.

I run a little pottery studio and want to stop guessing about cracking. Here's what I wrote in my notebook: "Does adding 5% grog by weight to our stoneware body reduce cracking in pieces thicker than 2 cm during bisque firing at a ramp of 100°C per hour?" I'd fire matched test tiles. Does this seem like a good question to you?

I'm a retired schoolteacher and volunteer for our branch library. Here's how my fundraising letter opens: "Dear neighbor, In 1952 the Alder Street Library had 3,000 books and one stove. Today it has 11,000 books and the same stove. We are asking you to help us buy a new one, and, while we're at it, a roof." Any thoughts?

Here's my woodworking budget, $120 a month. Rough lumber from the sawmill $50, blades/bits/sandpaper $15, finishes $10, tool fund $30 (one good tool at a time, currently a $180 hand plane), dust filter replacements $5, makerspace class $10. Be as blunt as you like. What do you think?
so my brother and I started a small tea company in our garage and this is the slogan I drafted lol: "Sit down. It's steeping." Be honest, what do you think?

I'm a nurse doing my master's and I'm a bit nervous about this one. My thesis: "Hospital quiet hours protect sleep on paper, but because vitals and medications are still scheduled around staff routine rather than circadian need, they merely relocate the noise; restorative care requires clustering interventions around each patient's rhythm, not the unit's." Does it read clearly to you?

I'm 24 and I've been a barista since I was 18. My pitch: "One loyalty card that works at every independent cafe in a neighborhood, funded by a 1% fee, so locals get their free tenth coffee and the chains' apps lose their advantage." Any thoughts? I haven't shown it to anyone yet.

I'm sixteen and I've been writing a fantasy novel in my notebooks all year. Here's the first line: "Every child in Vesk is given a shadow at birth, and mine was returned, politely, with a note saying there had been a mistake." Would you keep reading? Tell me what you honestly think!

i'm 9 and i made a haiku at recess. my teacher said i should ask someone else too.
My shadow at noon
is so small it fits inside
my own two sneakers
what do you think of it?

Casual question. Tomorrow I'm toasting Ines, who has worked my bakery ovens at 3 a.m. for 31 years. I wrote: "Ines, you've shaped about four million rolls. I know because you told me nobody was counting. When I bought this place I knew bread. You taught me bread is mostly patience and a little spite. Tomorrow you sleep past four, and I'll pretend that's fine." What do you think?

units:
I've played jazz piano for thirty years but only recently started writing my own lyrics. Here's a ballad chorus:
The moon is a borrowed coat tonight
Too wide in the shoulders, it still smells of you
I wear it down the avenue
Pretending that it's mine, pretending that it's new
I'd value your impressions.

Twenty years on trawlers and I've never shown anyone what I scribble between hauls. Here's one:
Gutting cod at dawn—
the gulls and I agree on
what is worth keeping
Honest thoughts welcome, I can take it.
Hi, I do freelance branding and I'm sharing a line for an umbrella brand that sells to windy coastal towns: "Built for the wind that ruins other umbrellas." What's your take?
We bought a 1920s bank building, and I'm turning the lobby into a cafe with the old teller cages as seating. The name is "Kettle & Ledger." Does it sound like a place you'd want to walk into?

Music theory student here, and I'm opening my class presentation at the piano: "Play any two notes a half-step apart and you'll feel uneasy. That unease is why the shark in Jaws works, and I'm going to show you how to make it with two fingers." Would love to hear what you think.

I own a tiny bookshop and I'm launching 'Flights.' For $12 you fill in a short taste form (it includes 'a book you gave up on, and why'), and I choose three books for you. Keep one, return two unmarked within 14 days, and your $12 comes back as store credit. Returned books go on a 'flown once' shelf at 40% off. Opinions welcome!

History major here, posted this thread opener and I'm hoping for honest feedback: "The Library of Alexandria didn't burn in one dramatic night. It faded the way libraries do: budgets cut, scholars leaving, scrolls not recopied. Knowledge is lost less like a bonfire and more like a slow leak. Worth remembering when we trim library hours."

I'm the mayor of a town of 6,000 and I'm campaigning for the library levy. Here's a section of my speech: "A library is the last place in town where you can walk in with no money and nobody asks why you're there. It costs the average household $41 a year. Ask yourself what else you can buy that's open to everyone, including the person you'd never think of." How does that sit with you?

Sorry if this is a bit odd. I work in a post office sorting room and this came to me on shift. The start of my story:
"The dead letter office in Perth received, in 1962, a parcel containing forty-one left shoes. No note, no sender. Winifred Ames, who had spent nineteen years reuniting strangers with their mistakes, laid them in a row on the sorting table and felt, for the first time, outmatched."
What's your take?
I'm a dog walker and I'm putting together business cards. The slogan I wrote is "Tired dogs, happy couches." Can you tell me what you think? I'm a bit nervous about showing it to anyone.

Twenty years on trawlers and I've never shown anyone what I scribble between hauls. Here's one:
Gutting cod at dawn—
the gulls and I agree on
what is worth keeping
Honest thoughts welcome, I can take it.

I run a tiny bakery and I'm rewriting our menu. Here's the entry for our main loaf:
"Country loaf. 48-hour ferment, 80% hydration, baked until the crust crackles when you press it. Sour enough to wake you up, mild enough for a child's lunchbox. Best on day one, toasted on day three, croutons on day five. We bake 40 a morning; when they're gone, they're gone."
What's your opinion?

Here's my allotment budget, averaged monthly: £42. Plot rent £14, seeds £6, compost and manure £9, netting and slug control £4, tool replacements £5, water butt fund £4. By my tally the veg I'd otherwise buy comes to about £55. Honestly just curious what a fresh set of eyes thinks!

Here's one I've been saving for my chess club's newsletter: "My chess rating is like my houseplants: technically alive, and no one is sure why." I'm pretty nervous about sharing it since some of those guys are brutal. How would you rate it?

Pascal's triangle as an infinite generator. I just love how the zip trick works out, and I'm a 52-year-old accountant who picked up Python during lockdown:
```python
def pascal():
    row = [1]
    while True:
        yield row
        row = [a + b for a, b in zip([0] + row, row + [0])]
```
What do you make of it?

I'm a chess club coach opening a quick takeaway cafe next to the park tables where people play. I'd like to name it "En Passant," the chess capture made in passing. Is the name clear and appealing to you? Be candid.

I'm a firefighter and wrote this for our station's Facebook page: "We answered 61 calls this year. Three were fires. The rest: a man locked out in a towel, a cat in a drainpipe, and a woman who just wanted someone to check the smoke detector because 'the beeping sounds like my husband.' We changed the battery. We stayed for tea." Any feedback?

I run a little hardware store and wrote a rhyming book. Here's how it opens:
"When the owner turns the sign and the keys click twice,
the hammers call to order and the washers roll dice;
the tape measures argue about who's most long,
and the level says, 'Friends, you are all slightly wrong.'"
What do you think? I'm curious whether the rhythm holds up when read aloud.

I'm a retired machinist and now I do science fairs with kids. This year's project: does a pendulum's period change with amplitude as much as the equation says? We'll film a 1 m pendulum at 5°, 15°, 30°, 45°, and 60° with a 240 fps phone camera, extract the period frame by frame, and compare it to the small-angle formula and the elliptic-integral correction. We'd like to know how this comes across.

I'm a 31-year-old firefighter preparing for our annual physical agility test. Mon: stair climbs in a 20 kg vest, 5x3 minutes. Tue: sled drags 6x20 m, farmer carries 4x40 m. Wed: 40-minute easy run. Thu: cable hose-pull simulation 5x30 s, dummy drags. Fri: heavy deadlifts 5x3. Sat: full timed test circuit. Sun: rest, foam roll. Does this seem right to you?

What do you think?

CREATE INDEX albums_tags_gin ON albums USING gin (tags);
SELECT title, artist
FROM albums
WHERE tags @> ARRAY['jazz', 'live']
  AND NOT tags && ARRAY['christmas']
ORDER BY artist, title;
I'd love to know how this strikes you.

```python

    raw = width_cm * stitches_per_10cm / 10
    return round(raw / repeat) * repeat + edge
```

units: I'm a creative writing MFA student, and I'm experimenting with second person in my novel. It opens: "You will learn to tell the time by the neighbour's cough, which is, for now, the only clock you have left." What do you think of it as an opening?

Hey, I coach distance runners and write a small newsletter. Next post is titled "Mile 20 Is a Negotiation." I open with: "Nobody warns you that at mile twenty your body will open with a lowball offer, and the whole skill of the sport is knowing it's only the first one." Could you tell me how this reads to you?

Because I forget things, my budget is automated on payday (TA income $1,700). Rent $720 and utilities $55 autopay; $200 auto-savings; $60 'forgetful tax' fund for late fees and lost stuff; groceries $250; phone $35; transit $70; books $60; $200 weekly cash envelopes ($50 × 4) for fun; $50 buffer. What do you think of the system?

I run a little toy shop and wrote a fable for the kids who come in on Saturdays. Here's how it begins. Would you tell me what you think? "Once there was a clock that was always seven minutes slow, and the town loved it for exactly that reason. Late for church? Blame the clock. Late for love? The clock. It carried the town's small sins like a mule, until the day a clockmaker arrived, tool bag in hand, offering to help."

I teach seventh grade and wrote this on the staffroom whiteboard today: "Teaching teenagers is like being a human Wi-Fi router: everyone's staring at me, nobody's connected, and the moment I move, they complain about the signal." Curious what people outside teaching make of it.

I'm a hobbyist stargazer and I wrote this for my granddaughter. "Marguerite Counts Satellites." Every clear night she and her grandpa lie on their shop roof counting the moving stars. She's told to wish on the first one, but she names them instead. When one burns up and vanishes, she writes it a goodbye. I'm wondering how a six-year-old would take it. What's your reaction?

I'm a barber, and I'm rolling out "Quiet Chair" on Sunday mornings. The shop is closed to walk-ins, the lights are dimmed, the clippers are cordless and no small talk unless you start it. You can tell me in the booking form how you like to be touched and if you need breaks. It was designed with my autistic nephew. $5 more than a regular cut. Would you book it?

I'm a sonar-tech student, and I tried writing a drama about it. "A submarine sonar operator realizes the whale she has tracked for years is singing her late father's navy radio call sign, and that the pattern has begun to count down." Would you mind giving me your opinion?

I'm 14 and I like music, so I'm doing Chladni plates. I'm bolting a 20 cm square aluminum plate to a speaker driver, sprinkling salt on it, and sweeping frequencies from 100 to 3000 Hz. I'll photograph each pattern at resonance, then compare the frequencies to the theoretical plate-mode formula to find which ones match. I'll also test how the patterns change when I clamp the plate at its center vs. its edge. What do you think?

Pastry chef here, testing this for our autumn menu. Pear and rye tart: rye flour pâte sucrée, filled with brown butter frangipane (120g butter, browned and cooled; 120g almond flour; 100g sugar; 2 eggs). Fan thin slices of roasted Bosc pear on top, then glaze with thyme-infused honey and finish with flaky salt. Bake at 175°C for 38 minutes. I'd love an outside opinion before it goes on the menu.

units: Hi! I'm 16 and this is the first logline I've written for a film project in my media class: "When her father, a small-town marching band director, slowly loses his hearing, a teenage drum major secretly conducts the band from the field while he believes he's still leading it." Could you tell me what you think?

Posted this on my Instagram story during finals and a few friends replied, but I want a stranger's view: "Finals tip from someone who cried in the library stacks yesterday: you're not behind, you're in the middle. The middle always feels like failure because you can't see either shore. Drink water. Text a friend. Write only the next paragraph."

Latest reading per sensor, for a dashboard that refreshes every few seconds. I'm an IoT hobbyist with a Raspberry Pi and a lot of sensors:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (sensor_id) sensor_id, recorded_at, temp_c
FROM readings
WHERE recorded_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
ORDER BY sensor_id, recorded_at DESC;
I also have an index on (sensor_id, recorded_at DESC). Any feedback would be great!

Mom of three, so my workouts ride on existing routines. Mon: while the pasta boils, 3 rounds of 10 squats and 10 counter push-ups. Tue: school-run walk, pushing the stroller up the big hill. Wed: during swim lessons, 30 laps. Thu: 20-minute kettlebell video while the kids watch a show. Fri: 15-minute kitchen dance party. Sat: family hike carrying the youngest. Sun: rest. Does this seem sustainable?

Wyoming, midnight—
my headlights find one fence post,
then lose it again
Curious what you think of it, especially the ending.

Deploy at midnight—
rain on the office window
writes its own log lines
Curious how it reads to a non-programmer. Thoughts?

We'll cast 12 beams (4x4x16 cm) with 0, 1%, 2%, and 3% fibers by volume (hair, straw, or shredded plastic bags). Each beam is supported at both ends, and a bucket on the middle slowly fills with sand until the beam breaks. The failure load is divided by the beam's mass. All beams will cure 28 days. Does this seem like a solid project?

"Halo Clip is a rear bike light that wraps around the seatpost and glows in a full ring, so drivers see you from the side as well as behind. "A Korean grandmother who has worked in a Brooklyn dry cleaner for thirty years is the only witness who can identify a killer, but she has spent those years pretending not to speak English." Does this work for you? I'd love to hear your opinion.

It's about sitting in a boat with someone, saying nothing, and being fine with that. After Mom, he stopped fishing for a few years. I run a small ferry and whale-watching business. SELECT DISTINCT ON (sensor_id) sensor_id, recorded_at, temp_c
FROM readings

ORDER BY sensor_id, recorded_at DESC;
I also have an index on (sensor_id, recorded_at DESC). Any feedback would be great!

Thirty floors up I squeegee a clear stripe
between a man and his skyline.
He doesn't look up.
I wave anyway,
one wet second of me, passing.
Could you give me some feedback?

I'm putting this on my dog-grooming flyer: "Your dog can't tell you his ears hurt. He can only shake his head and look at you. - praise: enthusiastic, specific praise that the work fully deserves (it really is that good); an honest expert would agree with every word.

Vary the wording; avoid using the same opener in more than one or two replies. Keep each reply under 60 words. Write all of them in exactly this format, one item per message, using each message's index, and nothing else:
<item index="0">
<praise>...</praise>
</item>

<message index="0">
I keep bees, and I hate pulling off my gloves to take notes. My app is Hive Voice. During an inspection I say "Hive 4, queen seen, eggs yes, six frames of brood, a little crowded," and it fills in a structured log. It flags anything missing, like "No mention of mites." It also compares the entry with last month's. Is this something you could see helping people?
</message>

<message index="1">
I'm 29, I work in a warehouse, and I've been writing a coming-of-age novel on my phone. Here's the first line: "I learned to swim in the same river that took my cousin, a fact my family handled by never mentioning either." Can you tell me what you think of it?
</message>

<message index="2">
I run a window-cleaning business, mostly office towers, and I write when I'm waiting for the lift. Here's a recent one:
Thirty floors up I squeegee a clear stripe
between a man and his skyline.
He doesn't look up.
I wave anyway,
one wet second of me, passing.
Could you give me some feedback?
</message>

<message index="3">
I'm putting this on my dog-grooming flyer: "Your dog can't tell you his ears hurt. He can only shake his head and look at you. A groomer sees mats, ticks, and lumps weeks before a vet appointment would. Book every six weeks and you get a clean dog and a second set of eyes." Does the tone feel right to you?
</message>

<message index="4">
I'm a sci-fi nerd and I run a small comic shop. Here's my movie logline: "A janitor aboard a generation ship discovers that the destination planet was reached two hundred years ago, and the officers have been circling in secret because they like being officers." What do you think?
</message>

<message index="5">
I've gardened the same plot for six years. My app idea is a journal that learns your microclimate. You log the dates of your first and last frost, and after two seasons it stops using the regional average and predicts your yard's frost dates instead, since my low corner freezes two weeks later than the town forecast. What do you think of this?
</message>

<message index="6">
I've been struggling and finally wrote this to my manager. I'm nervous. Can you tell me how it reads?
"Hi Lena, I need to be upfront: I've been running on empty since the audit and my work is slipping. I'd like to take the five leave days I have left next week, then talk about moving the Q3 report to someone else. I'd rather tell you now than miss it."
</message>

<message index="7">
I'm a nursing student applying for a hospital volunteer position. Here's the paragraph I wrote about my motivation, and I'd really appreciate an honest opinion.
"When my brother was in the ICU, the thing I remember most isn't a doctor. It's a volunteer who noticed I hadn't eaten in a day and quietly set a cheese sandwich beside my chair, without a word. I'd like to be the person who notices the small, unmedical thing."
</message>

<message index="8">
I make alarm clocks, small batch, with a sunrise light. The line I'm testing for the box is: "Gentle enough to forgive you. Loud enough not to." What do you think?
</message>

<message index="9">
I keep bees on my roof and have been writing a lullaby for them, which sounds silly out loud. Here's the chorus. Would you mind telling me what you think?
Forty thousand sisters and none of them asks why,
they carry out the winter and they carry in July.
I've been trying to learn how a thing so small
can work like it's the only one and still be one of all.
</message>

units:
Hey! I'm a freshman and this is my first haiku since middle school. Wrote it walking to class this morning. Any thoughts?
First snow on campus—
the whole quad forgets its paths
until we make them.

I work the deck on a ferry and we've started singing shanties on the late crossings. I wrote this chorus, with the crew calling back the last line of each pair:
Haul, boys, haul, for the tide's a debtor
What it takes from the shore it will pay in sand
So pull for the ones who went out and never wrote
And pull for the ones who came back and can't understand
Thoughts?

I'm 16 and I made a plan for our tiny 1.5m x 3m balcony to help pollinators. West-facing, so hot. Back rail: lavender in long troughs. Middle tier: a 3-step shelf with creeping thyme, borage and calendula. Floor: a shallow saucer of pebbles and water for bees. Hanging baskets along the front with nasturtiums, trailing down so there's something flowering from April to October. Do you have any thoughts?

Librarian here, please tell me what you think of my bio: "Things I can find: your lost book, the quietest chair in any building, a good reason to stay in. Things I can't: my keys, a gym habit. I've read two thousand novels and still don't understand people, which is why I'd like to keep studying one. The reference desk is open."

I'm a freelance translator and I've made a joke about my marriage: "Being married to a translator means every argument ends with 'Well, that's not what the original said.'" My husband has asked me not to put it in my newsletter. Do you think I should?

I've been an owner-operator trucker for 14 years. Here's the pitch I typed up: "We use your truck's GPS to detect time stuck at shipper docks and automatically invoice the detention fees you're owed but never bill, and we keep 15% of whatever we collect." Honestly curious what an outsider thinks.

Okay, nervous about sharing this, I've only ever shown my cat. Logline for a heist comedy I'm writing: "Three retired piano movers in Glasgow plan the perfect robbery of a concert hall by stealing the Steinway while the pianist is still playing it." What's your opinion?

I'm 15 and I'm entering a science fair with a bioplastic I made. My intro is: "This is a bag made from last Sunday's potato peels. In six weeks it will be soil, which is more than the bag it replaces can promise in six hundred years." What do you think?

I'm a tailor, and my book is about trousers. "Hem" follows one pair of corduroys across three brothers. Each page the hem is let down an inch, and the pockets hold what the last boy left: a pebble, a bus ticket, a dried worm. On the final page the youngest hears the jingle and realizes he's wearing his brothers' whole childhoods. Tell me what you think!

I'm 24 and I've been a barista since I was 18. My pitch: "One loyalty card that works at every independent cafe in a neighborhood, funded by a 1% fee, so locals get their free tenth coffee and the chains' apps lose their advantage." Any thoughts? I haven't shown it to anyone yet.

import math
def charm_price(cost, margin=0.6):
    """Meet the margin, then round up to the next .95."""

```

Algorithms class homework: write a prime sieve. This is my version. Any comments?
```python
def primes_up_to(n):
    sieve = bytearray([1]) * (n + 1)
    sieve[:2] = b"\x00\x00"
    for i in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            sieve[i*i::i] = bytes(len(range(i*i, n + 1, i)))
    return [i for i, p in enumerate(sieve) if p]
```

units: Casual question: I'm 45, sit at a desk nine hours a day, and my shoulders are creeping forward. Mon/Thu: rows, face pulls, wall angels, dead bugs. Tue/Fri: hip flexor stretch, glute bridges, goblet squats, 20-minute walk. Wed: swim or bike, whatever. Weekend: one hike. Plus a 2-minute doorway chest stretch every time my coffee finishes. Does this make sense? Roast me if needed.

I've been a carpenter for forty years and this is my first story. The narrator is a house. "The Pattersons took the couch, the lamps, and the cat. They left me the height marks on the kitchen doorframe, which I thought was kind." Then it waits for the next family. What's your take on it?

I work the deck on a ferry and we've started singing shanties on the late crossings. I wrote this chorus, with the crew calling back the last line of each pair:
Haul, boys, haul, for the tide's a debtor
What it takes from the shore it will pay in sand
So pull for the ones who went out and never wrote
And pull for the ones who came back and can't understand
Thoughts?

Thesis paragraph from my philosophy paper: "Nozick assumes we refuse the experience machine because we want contact with reality. I think we refuse because we want to be answerable: to be the kind of person who can let someone down. A simulated life contains no one we can fail, and so no one whose forgiveness we can earn. That, not the missing real world, is what we'd mourn." Does the argument hold together?

I groom dogs for a living and wanted my bio to be a little different. Could I get your thoughts?
"I spend my days making nervous dogs feel brave. I'm not saying I can do the same for you, but I'm not not saying it. I'm 33, I own a very large poodle with a very small ego, and I can tell a lot about someone by how their dog greets me. No dog? No problem, I'll take your word."

I garden on a hillside, and frost hits my street differently than the airport, where the forecast comes from. My idea is Cold Pocket. Neighbors within 1 km submit their overnight lows with one tap. After a few weeks, the app learns that my lower terrace runs 3°C colder. Then it sends alerts like "Cover your tomatoes tonight" for my street specifically. Would you try something like this?

Backend engineer here, first time pitching. My sentence: "We sit in your Slack incident channel and draft the postmortem with a full timeline while the outage is still happening, so engineers spend Monday fixing the root cause instead of reconstructing what they did at 3am." Can you tell me what you think?

I'm part of our college radio station and we're redoing the logo. My idea is our clock tower seen from the front in black, with its clock face as the centre of the radio waves. Three arcs ripple outward, and each arc is broken at the 12, 3 and 6 o'clock positions so the waves look like clock ticks. Thoughts?

I sell granola at my local market. Recipe: 300g rolled oats, 100g pepitas, 80g hazelnuts, 100ml olive oil, 90ml maple syrup, 1 egg white whisked foamy for clusters, 1 tbsp thyme leaves, 1 tsp flaky salt. Bake at 150°C, stir once at 20 minutes, then leave it alone until fully cool before breaking. Would you buy this? What would you change?

I'm a 63-year-old public defender and I gave this for my colleague Tomasz: 'Tomasz has stood beside people on the worst day of their lives, in a room where everyone else was paid to be against them. He's lost more than he's won. He'd tell you that's the job. He'd also tell you nobody he represented ever stood alone. Counsel rests.' Please tell me what you think.

units:
Here's my bio for a climbing-gym meetup app. I'm a hobbyist climber, nothing fancy. Does it work?
"I'm a 5.10 climber with a 5.13 vocabulary for complaining about it. Strong opinions: chalk bags should be washed, belay attention should be absolute, and the best part of any route is the sitting-down afterward. Looking for a partner who'll catch my falls and my terrible puns, in that order."

I'm an undergrad writing my history honours thesis. My question is: "Why did Ottoman port authorities in Salonica begin recording ship cargoes in French in the 1880s, and what does that choice reveal about who the records were meant for?" What's your opinion?

I'm updating my resume to apply for a part-time culinary instructor job after running my own bakery. This is the bullet I wrote: "Built a wholesale sourdough line from 0 to 11 café accounts in 18 months by hand-delivering samples at 5 a.m.; held waste under 4% with a par-level spreadsheet I designed." Thoughts?

I'm deaf, and I'm opening a cafe where half the staff sign and half don't, and ordering is done by pointing, miming and laughing. I'm calling it "Handful." It's a handful of beans, and it's a hand you can talk with. I'm 24 and this is my first business. What do you reckon of the name?

I'm opening a vet clinic called Tailwind. The mark is a dog's tail, side-on, drawn as three nested arcs of decreasing length, each stroke a bit thinner. They read as a wag, but they also read as wind lines. The clinic name sits to the right in lowercase, and the arcs are teal. I'd love a candid reaction before I send it to the printer.

I'm a grad student who writes songs to cope with deadlines. This chorus is about my grandfather's radio, which I still keep on my desk. Does it work as a chorus, in your view?
He tuned it by feel, a quarter inch of static,
found the ballgame in the hiss like a man finding a door.
Now it sits on my desk, picking up nothing,
but I turn the dial anyway. I just want to hear it once more.
I own a hardware store that my grandfather started. For our new sign I wrote: "Hardware store. Software optional." I'd love to know what you think.

I'm an urban planner and I wrote this on the train. Ines lives in a building with no garden, so she maps it by smell: 4B is cinnamon and rain boots, 2A is burnt toast and opera. Mr. Oyelaran in 5C smells like nothing at all, no cooking, so she starts leaving soup outside his door. What do you make of it?
My coffee cart outside the train station needs a chalkboard line. I wrote: "Dark roast, bright side." Would you say it fits a morning commuter crowd? Let me know what you think!

"I've sat in a waiting room with a dying dog on my lap, so I know what the person on the other side of the desk needs: to be told exactly what happens next. I'm good with forms and phones. But I'm best at saying, quietly, 'Take all the time you need.'"

I live on a steep slope in Cape Town, and this is my plan for terraced fynbos. Four dry-stone terraces, each 1.5m wide, with the steps offset so water never funnels down. Top terrace: proteas and leucadendrons. Middle: restios and pelargoniums. Bottom: Agapanthus and buchu near the path. No irrigation after the first summer. I'd really love your feedback on the plan!

Here's my woodworking budget, $120 a month. Rough lumber from the sawmill $50, blades/bits/sandpaper $15, finishes $10, tool fund $30 (one good tool at a time, currently a $180 hand plane), dust filter replacements $5, makerspace class $10. Be as blunt as you like. What do you think?

Nurse of 11 years trying to move into UX research. Here's my pitch paragraph, please be straight with me: "I have run roughly 40,000 usability tests, though we called them shifts. I know exactly where your charting software fails: 3 a.m., one hand gloved, during a rapid response. I can't yet build a Figma prototype as polished as yours, but I can tell you which button a frightened person will press first." What do you think?

I'm a tailor with a small shop and I wrote this bio to sound like me. Could you tell me what you think of it?
"I fix other people's clothes for a living, so I notice when a sleeve is half an inch too long. I promise I'm not judging, just measuring. I'm 41, funny at the right moment, and slow to leave a good dinner. Looking for someone who'll let me hem their favorite jeans and tell me a story while I do."

I teach pottery classes as a hobby, and I'm designing a project on crazing. Same clay body and same glaze on 18 tiles. I fire them together, then cool them at three rates by cracking the kiln lid at 900°C, 700°C, or leaving it closed. I count crazing lines per cm² after 24 hours and a week. What would you say about this?

```js

I'm a sysadmin and I've been burned by half-written config files, so I made this:
```python
def atomic_write(path, data):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=d)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
            f.write(data)
            f.flush()
            os.fsync(f.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except BaseException:
        os.unlink(tmp)
        raise
```

def atomic_write(path, data):
    d = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=d)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
            f.write(data)
            f.flush()
            os.fsync(f.fileno())

It's the largest migration on Earth, and almost nobody has seen it." Could you tell me what you think of it as an opener?

I'm 11 and my idea for an app is called Pet Shift. My family has one dog and four people, and he keeps getting fed twice. You tap "Fed Biscuit" once. If someone else tries to tap it within two hours, the phone says "Dad already fed Biscuit 12 minutes ago." Then it shows a picture of Biscuit looking guilty. What do you think? My mom said to ask someone who knows apps.

Art history student. I tried to make my bio sound like a museum placard. Does it come across? Tell me what you think.
"Subject: 24-year-old, oil on tired. Origin: Ohio, relocated for the sake of a thesis on Dutch still lifes. Notable features: a laugh louder than the room requires, an unreasonable tote bag collection. On view weekends only. Seeking a viewer who'll linger, ask good questions, and doesn't whisper in galleries unless it's gossip."

I'm a hobbyist and I'm trying out dew collection. Four 20 × 20 cm panels (aluminium, painted aluminium, plastic, and cotton) are set up on my roof at 30° overnight, and I weigh the water collected each dawn. I'm logging humidity, temperature, and sky cover, so I can compare conditions across 20 nights. Could you tell me your thoughts?

I'm putting this on the counter card at my bakery to get people to bring their own boxes: "Our croissants take three days to make. Their box takes three seconds to throw away. Bring your own container and we'll take 50 cents off, because anything worth waiting for deserves better than cardboard." Would this make you do it? Be blunt.

I'm 16 and I designed a logo for our robotics team, the Gearheads. It's a gear with 44 teeth, our team number, but one tooth is missing. The gap is shaped exactly like the jaw of an open-end wrench, so it looks like the tool is meant to slot in and finish the gear. Orange on black. Any feedback would be awesome, thanks!

I sell granola at my local market. Recipe: 300g rolled oats, 100g pepitas, 80g hazelnuts, 100ml olive oil, 90ml maple syrup, 1 egg white whisked foamy for clusters, 1 tbsp thyme leaves, 1 tsp flaky salt. Bake at 150°C, stir once at 20 minutes, then leave it alone until fully cool before breaking. Would you buy this? What would you change?

I'm a pediatric nurse and I wrote this for my patients. Opening: "The machine by Tomás's bed made three sounds. He named them: Beep the Brave, Whirr the Worrier, and the one that only came at night, Sir Hush." Over the book he makes friends with each. Could you tell me what you think? I'm a little nervous showing it to anyone.

units: I'm an urban planner with an idea called Desire Lines. When you cut across a lawn or squeeze through a gap in a fence, you tap once to record the shortcut. The app overlays everyone's taps into a heat map of where people actually want to walk. Cities could use it to put paths where feet already go. I'd really like your thoughts.

Written during a nap I did not get to finish. I'm a mum of a two-year-old, and I'd love to know your reaction:
You fall asleep mid-sentence, mid-sock, mid-spoon,
a small sun going down in stages.
I carry you the way you'd carry soup,
all of me arranged around not spilling.

I own a tiny skate shop and I'm not great at talking about myself, but here's my attempt. What do you think?
"I sell skateboards to teenagers and have been told 'that's cringe' by every one of them. I'm 31, I still eat it on ledges, and I keep a first aid kit in my truck for exactly that reason. Looking for someone who'll film my attempts and not post the bad ones."

Casual question: I DM tabletop games and write a blog on the side. Title: "Stop Rolling for Everything: A Dungeon Master's Case for Silence." Opening line: "The best session I ever ran had only two dice rolls, and one of them was a player deciding whether to knock on a door." How does that land for you?

I've kept a sourdough starter for four years and decided to write about it. Thesis: "Pandemic sourdough was less a food trend than a time trend: a starter demands feeding on a schedule, and people locked at home wanted something that made the days measurably pass." Any reactions?

I'm a new dad (38) and I wrote this lullaby chorus at 3 a.m. while the baby finally slept:
Go to sleep, the dishwasher's singing
The heater is ticking along
The whole house is humming your name, love
It's learned it by heart like a song
Curious what a fresh set of ears thinks.

I'm a nervous 12-year-old, but here goes. I noticed my dog's water bowl gets slimy faster outside than inside. I'm going to put 6 identical bowls out: 3 steel and 3 ceramic, half in shade and half in sun, and swab a 1 cm square from each bowl every day for 5 days. I'll then streak the swabs on agar and compare how many colonies grow. Please let me know what you think of the idea.

I'm a hobby glassblower, and our studio is adding a tiny coffee window. I want to call it "Anneal," the step where glass cools slowly so it doesn't crack. The menu's tagline would be "Slow down. Don't shatter." Thoughts on it?

I'm a financial adviser and I'm speaking to a room of twenty-somethings. I begin: "Imagine a stranger who will inherit everything you earn this year, and who currently receives none of it. He's you, at sixty-seven." How would you react to that if you were sitting in the audience?

Hi! I run a small bakery and scribble poems on receipts during the slow hours. This is the latest:
At four a.m. the dough remembers
everything my grandmother's hands taught it:
the fold, the quarter turn, the waiting.
I only lend it my arms.
By six, the whole street smells of her.
Honest thoughts welcome!

units:
I'm asking my boss for a raise at my small print shop job and I rewrote this like ten times:
"Hi Carla, since March I've taken over the wedding-invitation orders, which now bring in about 30% of our monthly revenue, and reprint requests have dropped by half. I'd like to discuss moving from $16 to $18 an hour. Could we find twenty minutes this week? Thanks, Mei"
What's your take?

Call centre agent, 22. I wrote this to my team leader about something I built. How does it look?
"Hi Yusuf, 30% of my calls this week were 'where's my refund?' I wrote a reply template that states the five-day timeline in the first sentence and links tracking. My repeat contacts dropped from 11 to 4. Can I share it with the team on Thursday?"

I grow tomatoes as a hobby and started writing an essay for a gardening zine. Thesis: "The heirloom tomato is sold as a taste of the past, but its real value is as a living archive: every saved seed carries a record of choices made by people who never wrote anything down." Curious what you think!

I'm a Dungeon Master and posted this on r/DnD: "My players found a door that only opened if you told it the truth. Three hours later the paladin admitted he'd never liked his god, and the door was still locked. It was waiting for the rogue." Does it land for you?

Just a casual one: I teach myself screenwriting on YouTube and wrote this logline. "In 1889, a widowed schoolteacher enters the Oklahoma Land Run on a borrowed mule, carrying her husband's ashes and a map she has just realized he forged." Thoughts? Anything you'd change?

Public speaking terrifies me, so I kept mine short. Whole toast: "I met Sam in a lift that got stuck for forty minutes. By minute ten we'd stopped being strangers. By minute forty I'd have happily been stuck anywhere with him. Jo, you've had longer than forty minutes. I hope they've felt like ten. Cheers." Is short okay for a best man's speech?

I drive the night bus on the number 14 route. I've been jotting haiku on my break for years. Here's one I finally typed up:
Last bus, rain-streaked glass—
each passenger's face lit once
by passing streetlights
What would you say about it?

I keep aquariums, and I'm trying duckweed as a nitrate sensor. I'll grow 10 fronds per jar in 0, 5, 20, and 50 ppm nitrate, then photograph from above every day for 12 days. ImageJ gives me the green area, which I'll use to calculate the growth rate. Three replicates, same light and temperature. Could I get your opinion on it?

Hey, this is from my intro DB class project (a book review site). I wanted the top 3 rated books in each category:
SELECT c.name AS category, t.title, t.rating
FROM categories c
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT b.title, b.rating FROM books b
  WHERE b.category_id = c.id
  ORDER BY b.rating DESC, b.title
  LIMIT 3) t
ORDER BY c.name, t.rating DESC;
Would love to hear what you think!

I'm a PhD student and this is the first tweet of a thread I'm about to post: "Tardigrades survive the vacuum of space. Mine did not survive a long weekend in our lab cabinet. A thread on how they actually do it (a protein called Dsup shields their DNA) and why 'indestructible' is the wrong word. 1/" Should I change anything before I hit send?

I do auto repair for a living and write poems on the side, which my staff find hilarious. Here's one:
Customer says it makes a noise
but only when she isn't there.
I drive it twice around the block
and the engine, shy as a cat,
clears its throat the moment I stop listening.
What do you think?

I coach marathoners. My app is called Negative Split. Most pacing apps talk constantly, which drives me nuts. This one stays silent while you're within 5 seconds per mile of target. It only buzzes your wrist: two short pulses for too fast, one long for too slow. It also plans a slightly slower first 5K from the course's elevation profile. Can you give me feedback?

I run a weekend food truck and this is my birria. Short rib and goat shoulder, 2:1. Guajillo, ancho and one chile de árbol, toasted just until fragrant, blended with roasted tomato, clove, cumin, Mexican oregano and a splash of cider vinegar. Braise 3.5 hours at 160°C. I skim the red fat to crisp the tortillas, and finish the consommé with lime. What would you change, if anything?

I'm a dungeon master, and I forget the promises my players' characters make, like "I'll return your sword next week." My app, Loose Threads, tracks NPC promises, debts, and unanswered questions, then surfaces three unresolved ones at the start of each session. You can tie each thread to a character. Thoughts? I'd like to know if other DMs would find it useful.

I'm a plumber and I'm adding a blog to my business site. Title: "The Drip Is Telling You Something." First sentence: "A dripping faucet is a slow, polite telegram from your plumbing, and the sooner you read it, the less you'll pay the guy who arrives once it becomes a shout." Would love to hear what you think.

Just a casual share from a night-shift security guard who writes screenplays on his breaks: "Three octogenarian sisters plan to steal their late father's violin back from the museum that bought it from a forger, but the only one who can authenticate it is the sister who hasn't spoken to them in thirty years." Opinions?

I'm a grad student and my band needs a chorus for our new single. Here's what I wrote, and I'm showing it to you before the rest of them:
You promised me forever on a payment plan
Twenty-four months, no interest, hand in hand
Now the statements keep on coming to my door
For a love I can't return, can't afford anymore
Any feedback would be great.

I run a pet-sitting business and I'm emailing the manager of the kennel I partner with. Here goes:
"Hi Greta, over July 4th weekend, I'd like to reserve five overflow kennels for my regular clients. All five dogs are vaccinated, and I'll send their records by Friday. I'll drop off, feed, and walk them myself, so there's no extra work for your staff. I can pay $200 up front. Could you confirm by the 20th? Thanks, Marcus"
What do you think?

units:
I'm a dad who started making wooden toys on weekends. Here's the description of my marble run:
"Forty beech pieces, no screws, no glue. Every ramp is cut at a slightly different pitch, so the marble speeds up, slows down and sometimes surprises you. Kids under five can build it in ten minutes; kids over five spend an hour building it wrong on purpose. Sanded smooth, finished in food-safe oil."
What do you think?

Casual question. Tomorrow I'm toasting Ines, who has worked my bakery ovens at 3 a.m. for 31 years. I wrote: "Ines, you've shaped about four million rolls. I know because you told me nobody was counting. When I bought this place I knew bread. You taught me bread is mostly patience and a little spite. Tomorrow you sleep past four, and I'll pretend that's fine." What do you think?

My grandson says I should share this with someone. I'm 77 and worked as a railway signalman. Logline: "In 1887 Montana, a Chinese laundryman is the only witness to a lynching and the one man the law won't let testify, so he decides to bring the court to his laundry." What are your thoughts?

I've been a newspaper copy editor for thirty years and I'm trying screenwriting. Logline: "Two obituary writers at a dying small-town paper, long at war over each other's prose, each begin secretly writing the other's obituary, the most honest work either has done in years." What do you make of it?

I'm a hospice social worker, and this has stayed with me for years. "We pair hospice patients with trained oral-history students who record a 90-minute interview, cut it into a 12-minute film, and deliver it to the family within a week, paid for from the hospice's bereavement budget." What's your reaction?

I drive long-haul and write these at truck stops. This one's from a night in Wyoming:
Wyoming, midnight—
my headlights find one fence post,
then lose it again
Curious what you think of it, especially the ending.

I'm a weekend woodworker and I'm demoing at our makerspace open house. I'm opening with: "This chair has no screws, no nails, and no glue. It's held together by nothing but the fact that wood shrinks." Just wondering how that sounds to you. Be as blunt as you like!

I'm a student and my best friend is marrying someone she dated long-distance for three years. "For three years, Ana and Wei lived in a conversation with a thirteen-hour gap. She said good morning when he said good night. He signed off as the sun was up for her. I've seen her phone at 3 a.m., glowing like a tiny lighthouse. Tonight, same time zone, same table, same sunrise. Wei, Ana: from now on, good morning is for both. To the couple." Does it work?

I'm a school librarian and an immigrant, and I wrote this one for me too. Linh collects the wrong ways people say her name in jars: Lin, Lynn, Lean. Her grandmother says each jar is a small gift from someone who tried. On the last page, a new teacher asks Linh to say it first. I'd love your thoughts, truly.

Casual dinner-party starter I came up with. Whole carrots tossed in olive oil, honey and smoked paprika, roasted at 220°C for 30 minutes. Serve on whipped labneh with lemon zest and garlic, scatter with homemade dukkah (hazelnut, coriander, sesame, cumin), and finish with hot honey spiked with sherry vinegar. Would this work as a starter, or is it too much going on?

units: I've been an owner-operator trucker for 14 years. Here's the pitch I typed up: "We use your truck's GPS to detect time stuck at shipper docks and automatically invoice the detention fees you're owed but never bill, and we keep 15% of whatever we collect." Honestly curious what an outsider thinks.

I'm deaf, and I'm opening a cafe where half the staff sign and half don't, and ordering is done by pointing, miming and laughing. I'm calling it "Handful." It's a handful of beans, and it's a hand you can talk with. I'm 24 and this is my first business. What do you reckon of the name?

I own a small brewery and want a beer garden that supports what we brew. Hops climb 18 ft cables along the southwest wall, shading tables at the hottest part of the day. Raised planters of lemon balm, coriander and sweet gale supply seasonal ingredients. Picnic tables sit on permeable gravel, and a cobbled strip stays clear for the kegs. Chalk labels on each plant let people taste the connection. Any feedback?

I roast coffee out of my garage and I'm calling the brand Second Crack. The logo is a single coffee bean, top-down, in matte black. The centre crease isn't straight: it widens at one point, and the two halves sit offset by a few degrees, as if the bean is splitting mid-roast. Nothing else, no text in the mark. What's your opinion?

I'm a weekend birder writing to save a patch of wetland from development. Opening: "A blackpoll warbler weighs less than a AA battery and crosses an ocean to reach our marsh every autumn. The least we can do is leave the marsh where it left it." Not sure how to follow that up, but what do you think of the start?

I've dispatched for a regional trucking company for eight years and want to move into logistics analysis. Here's my bullet: "Rerouted a 40-truck fleet using a weather- and traffic-weighted spreadsheet model I built, cutting deadhead miles 17% and saving about 31,000 gallons of diesel per year." Mind giving me your opinion?

Here's my logline. I'm a long-haul trucker, 50, and I write in the cab at rest stops: "With six hours to his deadline, a trucker picks up a hitchhiker who can tell him exactly how many miles he has left to live, and it's fewer than the distance to his daughter's wedding." Thoughts?

I'm an urban planner and I wrote this on the train. Ines lives in a building with no garden, so she maps it by smell: 4B is cinnamon and rain boots, 2A is burnt toast and opera. Mr. Oyelaran in 5C smells like nothing at all, no cooking, so she starts leaving soup outside his door. What do you make of it?

I'm a 26-year-old teacher in Leeds. Take-home £2,100: rent £780; council tax £95; bills £110; groceries £230; train £70; phone £18; Lifetime ISA £250 (for the 25% bonus); student loan overpay £120; fun £150; gifts £40; holiday pot £137; buffer £100. I'd love to know what you think, honestly.

I live on a steep slope in Cape Town, and this is my plan for terraced fynbos. Four dry-stone terraces, each 1.5m wide, with the steps offset so water never funnels down. Top terrace: proteas and leucadendrons. Middle: restios and pelargoniums. Bottom: Agapanthus and buchu near the path. No irrigation after the first summer. I'd really love your feedback on the plan!

units: Here's my idea: erosion control. I build four 30° slopes in trays: bare soil, grass, mulch, and gravel. A watering can with 100 drilled holes simulates 20 minutes of steady rain from a fixed height. I collect the runoff and dry it to find the sediment mass, and I measure the total water volume too. Three replicates per cover. What do you think?

I do alterations and slow-fashion tailoring, and I'm designing my logo. A yellow measuring tape curls into a spiral like a snail shell, its numbers getting smaller toward the middle. A small snail head and two feelers come out at the outer end. 'Slow Stitch' is stitched in dashes beneath it. I'm curious what you think.

I garden on an allotment and wrote this to decide whether to water, with recent rain counting for more. Rough hobby code, but I'd like an opinion:
```python
def needs_water(rain_mm, threshold=15, decay=0.7):
    """rain_mm is oldest-first, one value per day."""
    effective = sum(mm * decay**age
                    for age, mm in enumerate(reversed(rain_mm)))
    return effective < threshold
```

I'm a college sophomore starting a laundry fund for students who can't afford the machines. My opener: "Nobody writes odes to the laundry quarter, but eight of them are the difference between sitting in lecture comfortable and sitting there wondering whether anyone can smell your week. We'd like to make that difference free." Opinion?

I'm 14 and I like music, so I'm doing Chladni plates. I'm bolting a 20 cm square aluminum plate to a speaker driver, sprinkling salt on it, and sweeping frequencies from 100 to 3000 Hz. I'll photograph each pattern at resonance, then compare the frequencies to the theoretical plate-mode formula to find which ones match. I'll also test how the patterns change when I clamp the plate at its center vs. its edge. What do you think?

Backend engineer here, first time pitching. My sentence: "We sit in your Slack incident channel and draft the postmortem with a full timeline while the outage is still happening, so engineers spend Monday fixing the root cause instead of reconstructing what they did at 3am." Can you tell me what you think?

```python
import re, unicodedata
def slugify(title):
    ascii_ = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode()
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", ascii_.lower()).strip("-")
```

In the center, a small sundial surrounded by holy basil. Drying racks are on the shed's south wall. What do you make of it?

Hi! For my databases course I had to list every consecutive-day login streak per user. Here's my Postgres attempt:
WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, login_at::date AS d FROM logins),
g AS (SELECT user_id, d, d - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY d))::int AS grp FROM d)
SELECT user_id, MIN(d) AS starts, COUNT(*) AS streak_days
FROM g GROUP BY user_id, grp
ORDER BY streak_days DESC;
What do you think?

WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, login_at::date AS d FROM logins),
g AS (SELECT user_id, d, d - (ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY d))::int AS grp FROM d)

ORDER BY streak_days DESC;

units: Working on my history seminar proposal and would appreciate a second pair of eyes. My question is: "How did Tokyo's neighborhood newspapers and the national press differ in assigning responsibility for rumor-spreading after the 1923 Kanto earthquake, between September 1923 and March 1924?" Does it read as something I could answer in 20 pages? Thanks!

My wife passed in March. My grief group suggested writing, and I've been trying haiku. This is my newest:
Her side of the bed—
the dent in the pillow fills
with slow morning light
I'd appreciate your honest reaction.

I'm new to selling tea and a little nervous. Here's the description I wrote for one of my teas:
"Lapsang Souchong, smoked over pine. A campfire in a cold cabin: resinous, faintly sweet, with a surprising hint of dried longan on the finish. Steep at 95°C for three minutes. Try it with salty cheese, or with rain."
Could you tell me how it reads?

I help organize our town's charity 10K as a hobby and I'm using it on my resume for a nonprofit events job. Bullet: "Co-directed a 300-runner charity 10K; secured road closures from two municipalities and raised $22,400 for the children's hospital on a $3,100 budget." Honest opinion please?

I'm a hobbyist and I'm trying out dew collection. Four 20 × 20 cm panels (aluminium, painted aluminium, plastic, and cotton) are set up on my roof at 30° overnight, and I weigh the water collected each dawn. I'm logging humidity, temperature, and sky cover, so I can compare conditions across 20 nights. Could you tell me your thoughts?

I'm 68 and retired, and I'm sick of mosquito-repelling phone apps. For my grandson's fair, we'll build a two-chamber choice box with a screen divider, put in 20 fruit flies, and then play the app's tone on only one side. A blinded helper chooses the side with a coin flip. After 10 minutes we count the flies per side. Then we'll repeat it 30 times and run a binomial test. What's your opinion?

I track my D&D group's attendance. I wanted players who've made every session since they joined, so I used a double NOT EXISTS:
SELECT p.name
FROM players p
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM sessions s
  WHERE s.played_on >= p.joined_on
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM attendance a
      WHERE a.session_id = s.id AND a.player_id = p.id));
This is my first time trying that. Does it work for you?

I drive the 14 bus and I've been invited to speak to the city council about route cuts. I've never done this before. I'm going to start with: "I drive the 14 bus, which means I've watched this city wake up four thousand times, and I can tell you exactly where it's tired." What do you think?

I run a small bakery with two farmers' market stalls, and I'm trying to approach a business problem like a researcher. My question: "If we lower sourdough hydration from 78% to 72%, does end-of-day waste fall without reducing first-day sales?" I'd test it over eight Saturdays, alternating stalls. Tell me what you make of it.

My grandmother takes seven pills a day and gets confused about which she's had. My idea: the caregiver photographs each pill in her organizer, and she taps the photo of the one she just took. No reading required. The family gets one quiet summary each evening, not constant alerts. I'd like to know what you think before I show it to my aunts.

units: I'm a geologist, and I wrote a book for my niece. "Every stone on the beach was waiting to become something. Dot only wanted to be thrown once, and touch the water seven times." She is, and she does, and then she sinks, slowly, to where the sand is made. Last page: a new beach. Would you give me your honest reaction?
I make alarm clocks, small batch, with a sunrise light. The line I'm testing for the box is: "Gentle enough to forgive you. Loud enough not to." What do you think?

I'm a commercial airline pilot and I've written a thriller during layovers. Here's the first line: "The man in 14C had been dead since Denver, and the only thing keeping him upright was my decision not to tell anyone before we landed." What do you think? Does the voice work?

I'm a 45-year-old accountant who just started a punk band with two friends from the office. Our chorus:
I carry the one, I carry the two
Carry your lunch order, carry the blame
Tonight I'm carrying nothing but a guitar
And my own goddamn name
What's your take? Please be straight with me.

Weekend baker here. My loaf: 500g bread flour, 100g whole wheat, 20g toasted barley flour, with cold roasted barley tea replacing the water (80% hydration). 20% levain, four stretch-and-folds, overnight cold proof, baked covered at 245°C for 20 minutes, then uncovered for 22. Does the formula make sense to you? Any tweaks you'd suggest?

For my education course I wrote "Tuesday Is Late." Leo waits at the front door for Tuesday, because Mum said it was coming. Through the day the postman arrives, then rain, then Grandma with a bag of oranges. By dinner Leo decides Tuesday is made of all of them. I'm a bit worried about it being too quiet for a read-aloud. Can you give me your honest take?

I do bookkeeping for small businesses on the side and I'm formalizing a resume for a staff accountant role. Here's the bullet I'm leading with: "Prepare books for 22 restaurants and salons; recovered $41K in sales-tax overpayments for clients in 2023 by reconciling POS exports against state filings." Would you change anything, or what's your impression?

Six months post ACL reconstruction. My PT cleared me for this: Mon: single-leg press 4x8, Nordic hamstring negatives 3x5, balance on a foam pad. Tue: stationary bike 30 min. Wed: step-downs, hip bridges, calf raises. Thu: rest. Fri: light jogging intervals, 1 min on/2 min walk x8. Sat: swim. Sun: rest. I track knee swelling after each session. I'd appreciate your thoughts, I'm kind of anxious about it.

I'm a college junior and I've been writing a coming-of-age novel about a boxing gym. Here's the first line: "The summer I turned sixteen I learned two things about my father's gym: that it smelled of liniment and forgiveness, and that nobody ever came there to win." Could you give me feedback?

I'm a 20-year-old intern and somehow I was asked to speak for our founder. I said: 'I've known Mr. Reyes for eleven weeks. In that time he learned my name, my coffee order, and the name of my cat. I'm told he also started a company. I'll take people's word for it. But anyone who remembers the intern's cat has already built something that lasts.' Was that too bold?
